### Description

Currently for the `azurerm_storage_account` resource the provider sets `cross_tenant_replication_enabled` to `true` by default.<sub>1</sub>

According to MS documentation<sub>2</sub>, as of Dec 15, 2023 the API creates storage accounts with that value as `false`


The provider should be updated to reflect the default behavior of the API and the portal.

azurerm_storage_account

"terraform import azurerm_role_definition" pulls null values for scope

Hello team,

I had a Team member show me a better way to structure my Terraform and pushing state to S3 and getting it into a local gitlab etc.
In doing so I lost the state file for my Azure custom roles, he said I can use the import function to sort this out.

Now this is were my issue comes, the import works fine but when I run Terraform plan it says 
azurerm_role_definition.customrole must be replaced
 scope              = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" # forces replacement
looking at the state file the entries for scope are null 
            "scope": null

and as defined here https://www.terraform.io/docs/providers/azurerm/r/role_definition.html

scope - (Required) The scope at which the Role Definition applies too, such as /subscriptions/0b1f6471-1bf0-4dda-aec3-111122223333, /subscriptions/0b1f6471-1bf0-4dda-aec3-111122223333/resourceGroups/myGroup, or /subscriptions/0b1f6471-1bf0-4dda-aec3-111122223333/resourceGroups/myGroup/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/myVM. **Changing this forces a new resource to be created.**

So its changing from "null" to a value and as such forcing a the role to be replaced. This would be fine but you cant delete the role because it is in use across multiple subscriptions.

workaround was to manual edit the state file to add the scope but that not ideal.

anyone come across this? googling i dont find direct link to this issue.

documentation on import of azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting resource

This is to report a correction on the online documentation of "azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting"

The original link of the Terraform documentation is here:
https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/monitor_diagnostic_setting#import

where it discusses how to import this resource from Azure if one already exists.  The documentation states:

=====================
Diagnostic Settings can be imported using the resource id, e.g. 

terraform import azurerm_monitor_diagnostics.example /subscriptions/XXX/resourcegroups/resource_group/providers/microsoft.keyvault/vaults/vault|logMonitoring
=====================

First of all, the import command should start out with "terraform import azurerm_monitor_diagnostics_setting".  
"_setting" must be there, because that is the actual resource type.

Also, PLEASE NOTE, there is a pipe character "|" between "vault" and "logMonitoring".   This pipe "|" should be preceded by an escape character, otherwise, it will be misconstrued by the OS as a pipe, which will cause the portion of the command before the pipe to be executed first, and then the result piped into the part after the "|" character.  Thus the whole command will result in failure.

If one is running this command on Windows command line, then the escape character is "^".  If you are on Linux, then it is back slash.  In either case, the example should read like this:

# on Windows
terraform import azurerm_monitor_diagnostics.example /subscriptions/XXX/resourcegroups/resource_group/providers/microsoft.keyvault/vaults/vault^|logMonitoring"

# on linux
terraform import azurerm_monitor_diagnostics.example /subscriptions/XXX/resourcegroups/resource_group/providers/microsoft.keyvault/vaults/vault\\|logMonitoring"

Please review and validate.  If what I stated above is accurate, please update the documentation.

```shell
│ Error: Invalid combination of arguments
(...)

╵
╷
│ Error: Invalid combination of arguments
(...)
│ "source_image_id": one of `source_image_id,source_image_reference` must be specified
```


### Expected Behaviour

There is a possible configuration on Azure (when VM needs to be created from existing disk by attaching it during creation process), that VM doesn't have a source_image parameters set at all. 
In that case source_image_reference is null and source_image_id = "" on Azure side and you have to be able to reflect that in terraform, otherwise terraform wants to re-create the whole VM.

Currently the only workaround we've found is to use some not existing, only visually proper source_image_id like the one in example configuration section ("" is not working because of parsing errors) and then add:
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [
      source_image_id
    ]
  }
So that terraform just ignore this section and is not trying to recreate.


### Actual Behaviour

Terraform errors out during parsing and doesn't want to proceed with empty source_image variables - which is incorrect given that it is allowed on Azure.
IMPORTANT: It was working correctly up to version 3.30.0, but I couldn't see any remarks about any changes within the resource in release notes after that

### Steps to Reproduce

Sorry, since this is a very specific scenario, it is impossible to provide exact steps, unless we include tons of powershell/az commands to prepare the environment first.
The easiest way to reproduce is to create a vm attaching the existing disks, then import in terraform, so that following command displays the same as below:
# tf state show  MODULE.azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.main | grep image
    source_image_id               = ""

and then create a base code for the VM and try to perform terraform plan WITHOUT any source_image_xxxxxx variables present in the code.
With <= 3.30 it will work, with 3.31 it will fail on dependencies.

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl

}

resource "azurerm_user_assigned_identity" "main" {
  name                = "uai-main"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.main.name
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.main.location
}

resource "azurerm_federated_identity_credential" "main" {
  name                = "fedid-name"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.main.name
  audience            = ["foo"]
  issuer              = "https://foo"
  parent_id           = azurerm_user_assigned_identity.main.id
  subject             = "foo"
}
```


### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Terraform will perform the following actions:

  # azurerm_federated_identity_credential.main must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_federated_identity_credential" "main" {
      ~ id                  = "/subscriptions/redacted/resourceGroups/resource-group/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/uai-main/federatedIdentityCredentials/fedid-name" -> (known after apply)
        name                = "fedid-name"
      ~ parent_id           = "/subscriptions/redacted/resourceGroups/resource-group/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/fedid-name" -> "/subscriptions/redacted/resourceGroups/resource-group/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/uai-main" # forces replacement
        # (4 unchanged attributes hidden)
    }

Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.
```


### Expected Behaviour

Because the `parent_id` attribute in the `azurerm_federated_identity_credential` resource was not changed, there shouldn't be a need to replace its value or recreate the resource. Running `terraform plan` or `terraform apply` should show the message "No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration."

### Actual Behaviour

Every time `terraform plan` or `terraform apply` are run, changes are detected in the `parent_id` attribute even though there **aren't any changes**, which triggers a replace operation on the resource. Also, the value for that attribute is incorrect in the plan output created by the state refresh. The `parent_id` read during the state refresh process is using `azurerm_federated_identity_credential.main.name` at the end of the resource ID string, instead `azurerm_user_assigned_identity.main.name` as the state, API and Azure portal reflect.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a `azurerm_federated_identity_credential` and note the `parent_id` passed and in Azure (it will match the required User Assigned Identity resource ID).
2. Run `terraform plan` or `terraform apply` without changing the infrastructure definition
3. Note that terraform will detect changes that require a replace operation because the refreshed `parent_id` attribute was not constructed properly by the provider when fetched form Azure (it will have the FederatedCredentialName at the end of the parent ID instead of the UserAssignedIdentityName as it should)

_No response_

### References

- In Azure's REST APIs, the [Federated Identity Credential resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/managedidentity/2022-01-31-preview/federated-identity-credentials/create-or-update?tabs=HTTP#uri-parameters) has two fields that are being mixed up in the provider when refreshing state from Azure. These fields are the `resourceName`, which should be used in the `parent_id`, and the `federatedIdentityCredentialResourceName`, which represents the credential name, but is currently being used to construct the `parent_id`.

### Description

Azure Virtual Networks now support in GA a feature called "Advertised gateway prefixes" (summarizedGatewayPrefixes) which allows customers to reduce the number of ranges advertised to On-premises network by specifying their own list of summarized ranges and overwrite what the SDN normally programs.

Public documentation can be found here:

### Description

To align our organization with the Azure Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) and adhere to Azure Policies, we've employed Terraform modules for streamlined network security and service deployments. A central aspect of this strategy is the deployment of vNet spokes connected to our central Hub. These spokes must support Microsoft Fabric and Container Apps, necessitating the ability to delegate subnets for seamless service integration.

Challenge with current separation between subnet and vNet resources

A key challenge stems from the Azure policy [Subnets should be associated with a Network Security Group](https://www.azadvertizer.net/azpolicyadvertizer/e71308d3-144b-4262-b144-efdc3cc90517.html). This mandates the attachment of Network Security Groups (NSGs) at the time of subnet creation. Due to this requirement, vNet creation becomes complex as it cannot proceed without pre-defined subnets and associated NSGs, demanding an integrated approach from the very beginning.

The current design of the azurerm_virtual_network resource presents a roadblock. It lacks support for configuring subnet delegation (recently implemented in this PR) and NSGs simultaneously. This limitation hinders many organizations' ability to comply with Azure's security best practices. The current design also prevents us from making this delegation a second day activity, because the subnet is now managed by an existing resource (as documented).

Potential Solution

A potential solution lies in extending the `azurerm_virtual_network` resource to enable delegation within subnet blocks. This enhancement would allow us to create vNets while simultaneously adhering to Azure's security policies.

```hcl
  address_space       = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.test.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.test.name

  subnet {
    name           = "test-subnet"
    address_prefix = "10.0.1.0/24"
    security_group = azurerm_network_security_group.test_nsg.id

    delegation {
      name = "acitestdelegation"

      service_delegation {
        name    = "Microsoft.ContainerInstance/containerGroups"
        actions = ["Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/action"]
      }
    }
  }

  tags = {
    environment = "Testing"
  }
}
```

### Terraform (and AzureRM Provider) Version

 ```
!terraform -v
Terraform v1.0.8
on linux_amd64

azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = "2.81.0"
    }
```

### Affected Resource(s)

<!--- Please list the affected resources and data sources. --->

* `azurerm_private_endpoint`

### Terraform Configuration Files


example of the resource
```hcl
resource "azurerm_private_endpoint" "storage_private_endpoint_primary" {
  ...
  subnet_id           = var.private_link_subnet_primary
  private_service_connection {
    name                           = "${var.name}-primary-service-connection"
    private_connection_resource_id = azurerm_storage_account.storage.id
    subresource_names              = ["blob"]
    is_manual_connection           = false
  }
  private_dns_zone_group {
    name                 = "privatelink.blob.core.windows.net"
    private_dns_zone_ids = [var.private_dns_zone_id]
  }
}

```

The subnet ID (`private_link_subnet_primary`) contains the subnet, but the resource group is lowercase instead of as it was created, with PascalCase.

### Expected Behaviour

Since resource groups are case insensitive, a "plan" following a "deploy" yields no change.

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/resource-name-rules#microsoftresources

Most Azure resource names are case insensitive and Terraform must respect this, since some of the APIs will not return the existing IDs in their canonical form (as in the example of the private link service lowercasing the resource group). I did not investigate if the casing of the other components of the ID causes similar issue, but I suspect so.

Also note that just lowercasing the string will not work as the service type etc are not lowercased.

### Actual Behaviour

The plan wants to recreate the resource, indicating that a change in subnet ID mandates force recreate. The diff between the old and the new string is just the casing of the resource group nae,s.

The problem is made worse by the fact that extracting the resource ID from a data resource. So it looks like this happens anytime I use non-lowercase resource group names unless I miss something.

Example output

```
# module.client_storage.azurerm_private_endpoint.storage_private_endpoint_primary must be replaced
    -/+ resource "azurerm_private_endpoint" "storage_private_endpoint_primary" {
   ...
~ subnet_id                = "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/my-resource-group/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/yyy/subnets/zzz" -> "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/My-ResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/yyy/subnets/zzz" # forces replacement
```


Working around this by setting

```
subnet_id           = replace(var.private_link_subnet_primary, ""My-ResourceGroup, "my-resource-group")
```
makes "terraform plan" work as expected (but this workaround is obviously very ugly to have in my .tf files)

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Please list the steps required to reproduce the issue. --->

1. Create a `azurerm_private_endpoint` with an explicit subnet ID, deliberately altering the casing of the resource group.
2. terraform apply
3. terraform plan

Observe that "terraform plan" shows the resource has to be recreated.

### Details

Two new fields introduced in the `terraform-provider-azurerm` 2.86.0 will force replacement of pre-existing storage accounts. To me this seems like an urgent bug - it means that v2.86.0 is not back-compatible, the change made to is breaking.

As part of 2.86.0, new fields have been added to the azurerm terraform provider with both `ForceNew` option + default value provided - it looks like this is forcing re-creation of resources that were created with old terraform provider.

e.g. in 2.86.0 the azurerm_storage_account resource has had new fields `queue_encryption_key_type` and `table_encryption_key_type`  added, both with ForceNew and with default values as "Service".

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/pull/14080/files

Now running this over my existing storage accounts, terraform will force re-create the resources since these new fields did not exist before, and they have ForceNew on them - the change from 'empty' to 'value' forces re-creation.
```
  # module.blobstore.azurerm_storage_account.efix_storage_account[0] must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_storage_account" "efix_storage_account" {
      + queue_encryption_key_type        = "Service" # forces replacement
      + table_encryption_key_type        = "Service" # forces replacement
...
}
```

### FIX

Proposed fix after discussing with @aristosvo : Remove the default value behaviour for the `queue_encryption_key_type` and `table_encryption_key_type` fields. Default will be empty unless specified during the initial create. Update tests and data source accordingly.

### PR for fix below:

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/pull/14278

### Expected Behavior

```
Success! The configuration is valid.
```

### Actual Behavior

```
C:\Users\gberesford\source\repos\OpenVpnRemote\testtf>terraform validate

Error: Error - only ssh-rsa keys with 2048 bits or higher are supported by azure

  on main.tf line 37, in resource "azurerm_linux_virtual_machine" "example":
  37: resource "azurerm_linux_virtual_machine" "example" {
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate 2048 bit RSA key with PuTTYgen.
2. Use public part of key for `public_key` in `admin_ssh_key` of `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine` resource.
1. `terraform validate`

### Important Factoids

PuTTYgen uses `37` as the RSA exponent, as opposed to ssh-keygen's `65537`. The shorter exponent means that it takes up less space in the encoded public key, which makes the byte indexes of 20 and 21 incorrect here: https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/2190f5565087143c6d67b05270685eda8d4f115d/azurerm/internal/services/compute/ssh_keys.go#L147

The current code will fail with any exponent < 65536 (or > 16777215 and also for some key lengths > 65535 but those cases are unlikely.)

I suspect the only reliable way of doing this will be to parse the file properly to skip the first 2 elements by reading their length (which are uint32s, not uint16s), and then read the length of the 3rd element.

### Description

Consider the scenario:

- I want to provision a virtual network, and a subnet to deploy Azure AD Domain Services (AADDS)
- AADDS hosts its own domain name servers which are to be set on the virtual network
- the `azurerm_virtual_network` has a property for setting DNS servers 
- the `azurerm_active_directory_domain_service` depends on the `azurerm_virtual_network` in order to deploy it

Because of this, there is a chicken:egg problem where I can't update the DNS servers because I don't technically know the IP. Granted, I know what subnet I am deploying it into, and could reasonably guess what the IPs it will allocate would be, but that seems fragile and prone to break

To solve this, I would like the ability to set DNS settings as a separate virtual network resource type, similar to how subnets are managed.

### Terraform (and AzureRM Provider) Version

<!-- this can be obtained from `terraform -v` -->

* Terraform Core version: 1.0.6
* AzureRM Provider version: 2.73.0

### Terraform Configuration Files

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

```hcl
resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "service_bus_connection_string" {
  name = "service-bus-connection-string"

  value        = azurerm_servicebus_topic_authorization_rule.mysb.primary_connection_string
  key_vault_id = azurerm_key_vault.main.id
}

resource "azurerm_function_app" "main" {
  name                = "myfn"
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.main.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.main.name

  app_service_plan_id = azurerm_app_service_plan.main.id

  enable_builtin_logging = true
  https_only             = true
  os_type                = "linux"

  storage_account_name       = azurerm_storage_account.main.name
  storage_account_access_key = azurerm_storage_account.main.primary_access_key

  version = "~3"

  app_settings = {
    AzureWebJobsServiceBus      = "@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=${azurerm_key_vault_secret.service_bus_connection_string.id})"
  }
}

```

### Description / Feedback

When the underlying value for an `azurerm_key_vault_secret` changes, the ID for the secret is generated. In the above code sample, the first time `terraform apply` is run, the app_setting is seeded properly with the resulting ID from the key vault operation with the version of the secret created. The `app_settings` config value will look something like: `@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://hmykv.vault.azure.net/secrets/service-bus-connection-string/809284ceae23484589eb0fa1a6c6e147)`

Again, on the initial first apply, this works as expected.

After changing the value (in our use case, rotating the primary access key of the access policy for the service bus account) however, the ID does not change on the 2nd apply. On the 2nd `terraform apply`, the value of the secret will be updated, but the `azurerm_key_vault_secret.service_bus_connection_string.id` reference will remain at the old value.

On a 3rd `terraform apply`, the secret version value in the attribute output reference will be properly updated.

### Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create config similar to above.
2. Run `terraform apply` - Observe that the use of the `id` attribute in `azurerm_key_vault_secret` is used correctly
3. Change the value of the `azurerm_key_vault_secret` 
4. Run `terraform apply`

**Expected**: The dependency on the `azurerm_key_vault_secret` updates the usage of the `.id` property such that dependencies on the secret in terraform are propagated and updated in their usages  
**Actual**: The value is updated in terraform, but the dependencies on the `.id` value of the `azurerm_key_vault_secret` do not reflect the new ID created in Azure. 

Workaround: Run `terraform apply` a third time, and the ID will get updated.

Consider splitting `azurerm_application_gateway` resource into several smaller ones

### Community Note

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request

<!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->

### Description

<!--- Please leave a helpful description of the feature request here. --->

I've been working with Application Gateway lately and wanted to defer some responsibility of configuring parts of Application Gateway to other teams. Right now, this is only possible by making the app gateway resource a giant, shared one, which everyone can change. I'd like to split the app gateway into several sub-resources, similar to what happened to IotHub resource: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/3303

I'd like to be able to define separate resources for backends, frontends, routing rules, health probes. This would reverse the dependencies between the app gateway and backend services, making the tf code more modular. Dependencies between sub-resources would also be much clearer. Now, they are only ensured by the consistent naming of the sections of app_gateway configuration. Splitting the resource would make those dependencies explicit and easier to get wrong.

Deployments would also be independent in a scenario where a single app gateway is shared by multiple teams. The teams can reconfigure the backends or routing as needed and apply their part of the infrastructure change without affecting other teams.

I am willing to gradually implement the resources, but want to get an OK/not OK from the maintainers.

## 3.49.0 (March 23, 2023)

BREAKING CHANGES: 
App Service `site_config`
* `ip_restriction` blocks are no longer computed - changes to IP restrictions outside of Terraform will now present a diff
* `scm_ip_restriction` blocks are no longer computed - changes to SCM IP restrictions outside of Terraform will now present a diff
* `cors` blocks no longer require `allowed_origins`, however, if the property is supplied it must contain at least one item. Omitting this property will set the array empty

BREAKING CHANGES:

* **App Service App Stack Re-alignment** - due to a number of changes in how the Service manages App and Stack settings, the Terraform resource schema and validation needs to be updated to re-align with the service. Whist we ordinarily avoid breaking changes outside a major release, the drift has made several aspects of these resources in an unworkable position resulting in a poor experience for many users ([#19685](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/19685))

* `azurerm_windows_web_app`
    * `node_version` Valid values are now `~12`, `~14`, `~16`, and  `~18`. This is due to an underlying change to where the Service reads the Node value from in the API request.
    * `dotnet_version` valid values are now `v2.0`, `v3.0`, `v4.0`, `v5.0`, `v6.0`, and `v7.0`
    * New setting `dotnet_core_version` - Valid values are `v4.0`. This setting replaces the hybrid setting of `core3.1` in `dotnet_version` since the removal of core3.1 from the supported versions.
    * `tomcat_version` - Configured the Web App to use Tomcat as the JWS at the specified version. See the official docs for supported versions. Examples include `10.0`, and `10.0.20`
    * `java_embedded_server_enabled` - configures the JWS to be the Embedded server at the version specified by `java_version`. Defaults to `false`. Note: One of `java_embedded_server_enabled` or `tomcat_version` is required when `java_version` is set.

* `azurerm_windows_web_app_slot`
    * `node_version` Valid values are now `~12`, `~14`, `~16`, and  `~18`. This is due to an underlying change to where the Service reads the Node value from in the API request.
    * `dotnet_version` valid values are now `v2.0`, `v3.0`, `v4.0`, `v5.0`, `v6.0`, and `v7.0`
    * New setting `dotnet_core_version` - Valid values are `v4.0`. This setting replaces the hybrid setting of `core3.1` in `dotnet_version` since the removal of core3.1 from the supported versions.
    * `tomcat_version` - Configured the Web App to use Tomcat as the JWS at the specified version. See the official docs for supported versions. Examples include `10.0`, and `10.0.20`
    * `java_embedded_server_enabled` - configures the JWS to be the Embedded server at the version specified by `java_version`. Defaults to `false`. Note: One of `java_embedded_server_enabled` or `tomcat_version` is required when `java_version` is set.

* `azurerm_windows_function_app`
    * `dotnet_version` - Valid values are now `v3.0`, `v4.0`, `v6.0`, and `v7.0`, defaulting to `v4.0`
    * `java_version` - Valid values are now `1.8`, `11`, and `17`

* `azurerm_windows_function_app_slot`
    * `dotnet_version` - Valid values are now `v3.0`, `v4.0`, `v6.0`, and `v7.0`, defaulting to `v4.0`
    * `java_version` - Valid values are now `1.8`, `11`, and `17`

* `azurerm_linux_web_app`
    * `java_version` - input validation has been introduced based on supported values within the service. Valid values are now: `8`,`11`, and `17`.

### Expected Behaviour

The `azurerm_key_vault_secret` is created successfully in one terraform apply sequence.

### Actual Behaviour

The `azurerm_key_vault_secret` fails to get created despite explicit dependencies. When testing with the example code, the apply will fail every time.

This completely breaks the workflow of creating a key vault and adding a secret to it. CD pipelines which require a single run deployment cannot be used.

*I have based my issue from #18659 which also outlines the same behaviour. It has not had any responses since it was created 3 years ago. I have tried getting attention on that issue instead, but have not heard anything, hence me raising this issue.*

## My setup 

I have changed original names to example all over and censored a number of details.

- The key vault created in the configuration above denies all public access from the internet for data plane operations
- Private access to the data plane is available via a private endpoint, which adds a private IP in the virtual network
- To access the private IP, I am running a VPN on my client machine that is executing Terraform
- The service principle/identity running Terraform is provided permissions to the key vault via access polices. I have also tried with IAM/RBAC

## First apply

1. On first apply, the key vault and private endpoint are created.
2. After these resources are created, a secret will attempt to be added. This fails with the following error.

```plaintext
│ Error: checking for presence of existing Secret "example-application-access" (Key Vault "https://example.vault.azure.net/"): keyvault.BaseClient#GetSecret: Failure responding to request: StatusCode=403 -- Original Error: autorest/azure: Service returned an error. Status=403 Code="Forbidden" Message="Client address is not authorized and caller is not a trusted service.\r\nClient address: <My local machine IP Address here>\r\nCaller: appid=<app id of the terraform user>;oid=<object id of the terraform user>;iss=https://sts.windows.net/<tenant id>/\r\nVault: example;location=<my location here>" InnerError={"code":"ForbiddenByFirewall"}
```

## Second apply

Applying for a second time will show that only the `azurerm_key_vault_secret` needs to be created and successfully creates it.

*Note that I do not change my networking configuration at all between the first and second applies.*

## Workaround

A workaround can be put in place using the `time_sleep` resource.

A 120 second sleep can be added after the PE is created, but before the secret is deployed. It seems somewhere between 60 - 120s is the sweet spot. See an example below, which just comments in some parts from the configuration above.

```hcl
resource "time_sleep" "wait_120_seconds" {
  create_duration = "120s"
  depends_on      = [
    azurerm_private_endpoint.keyvault,
    azurerm_key_vault_access_policy.example
  ]
}

resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "example_application_access" {
  name         = "some-secret-name"
  value        = "some-secret-value"
  key_vault_id = azurerm_key_vault.example.id
  
  depends_on = [
    time_sleep.wait_120_seconds
  ]
}
```

This will succeed in a single apply.

This is still not a great workaround, as it has a static timeout that could be exceeded. Additionally extra resources are created and dependency chains can become quite complex to work with.

In a [related item's comments section](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/18659#issuecomment-2821539273), you can find my suggestion on making this as easy to work with and neat as possible.

## Speculation

I guess the issue could be caused by some sort of DNS caching on the Terrraform client, or just that the private endpoint is returning an OK before it's actually finished it's configuration. Very difficult to know, without devs response.

Depending on the cause, some thoughts for possible long term solutions for the devs would be:

- An additional API request could be made to ensure the PE is fully configured before setting the Terraform resource as created.
- Somehow invoke a DNS cache refresh after creating a PE - I expect this one would be a real challenge to implement.
- Add an exception to the `azurerm_key_vault_secret` resource where it will retry at an interval for 120 seconds (or possibly lower), even if it cannot reach the host yet - not ideal, as there's still a chance it could exceed this duration.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the code from the configuration files without changing them to reproduce the error.

Comment in the advertised lines, as seen in the workflow section, to allow it to succeed with a workaround.

The storage account is created in Azure, but errors out in Terraform. Attempts to re-create the resource may fail during planning or apply.

After some additional research, I have determined that the culprit is the combination of the `shared_access_key_enabled` argument set to `true` and `restore_policy` inside the `blob_properties` block:

```hcl
restore_policy {
      days = 15
    }
```

Removing the `restore_policy` block will allows the storage account to be created successfully.


### Actual Behavior

Goal is to migrate existing disks into the new resource `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment` so that we can leverage count to attach multiple disks.   

Our existing VM's were created using: 

```
 storage_data_disk {
    name              = "${format("%s%03d", local.base_hostname, count.index + 1)}-datadisk1"
    create_option     = "Empty"
    lun               = 0
    disk_size_gb      = 5
    caching           = "ReadOnly"
    managed_disk_type = "Standard_LRS"
  }   
```

We then import disks using the following commands:

```
terraform import azurerm_managed_disk.data_disk /subscriptions/55546ce0-6c1c-40d0-98dd-007c68adfcd6/resourceGroups/USTV-Web/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/USTVlxyz001-datadisk1

terraform import azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment.data_disk_attach /subscriptions/55546ce0-6c1c-40d0-98dd-007c68adfcd6/resourceGroups/USTV-Web/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/USTVlxyz001/dataDisks/USTVlxyz001-datadisk1
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform init`
2. `terraform apply`
3.  After the creation you will have a VM with a disk which is attached.
4.  Run the above import commands to import the disk into the `azurerm_managed_disk` and `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment`
5. Comment out the `storage_data_disk` block in `azurerm_virtual_machine` 
6. Increment the variable `data_disk_count` to 1
7. `terraform plan` 

You will see that `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment.data_disk_attach` is forcing a new resource because of `create_option`:

```
-/+ azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment.data_disk_attach (new resource required)
      id:                        "/subscriptions/55546ce0-6c1c-40d0-98dd-007c68adfcd6/resourceGroups/USTV-Web/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/USTVlxyz001/dataDisks/USTVlxyz001-datadisk1" => <computed> (forces new resource)
      caching:                   "ReadOnly" => "ReadOnly"
      **create_option:             "Empty" => "Attach" (forces new resource)**
      lun:                       "0" => "0"
      managed_disk_id:           "/subscriptions/55546ce0-6c1c-40d0-98dd-007c68adfcd6/resourceGroups/USTV-Web/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/USTVlxyz001-datadisk1" => "/subscriptions/55546ce0-6c1c-40d0-98dd-007c68adfcd6/resourceGroups/USTV-Web/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/USTVlxyz001-datadisk1"

      write_accelerator_enabled: "false" => "false"

```

We can get around this by putting `create_option = "Empty"` on the `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment`.  However this doesn't help us.  Leaving  `create_option = "Empty"` will break adding any new disks, `attach` is needed to create new disks.    **Lets test this...**

8. Add  `create_option = "Empty" under `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment` 
9. `terraform plan` > You will see **no changes**.
10.  Increment the variable `data_disk_count` to 2.
11. `terraform apply` > You will see that `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment` changed for disk 1 which is another open GHI #1784 (ignore that).

Error: Error applying plan:

> 1 error(s) occurred:

>

> above and apply again to incrementally change your infrastructure.

We also tried modifying the state for existing disks which were marked as `Empty` > `Attach`, which didn't work.

This is blocking us on migrating large environments into the new resource `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment`.  We can't recreate these disks which is why we are forced to import them.

Any help or guidance would be appreciated.

### Description

We know 'azurerm_key_vault' resources supports an 'access_policy' block. like so:

```
resource "azurerm_key_vault" "akv" {
  for_each                        = var.key_vaults
  name                            = each.value.name
  ## other properties redacted
  access_policy {
    object_id = data.external.account_info.result.object_id
    key_permissions = [
      "List",
      "Get",
    ]
    secret_permissions = [
      "Set",
      "Get",
      "Delete",
      "Purge",
      "Recover",
      "List"
    ]
    certificate_permissions = [
      "List",
    ]
  }
}
```
And we can introduce many access_policies inside the azurerm_key_vault resource with a dynamic block (using a for_each + content loop).

Why can't we do the same for keys/secrets/certificates too?
After all there are two ways of creating access policies... (azurerm_key_vault_access_policy and the block defined inside azurerm_key_vault).  Yet with keys, secrets and certificates - we have only one method!


My thoughts on how this could be achieved:
```
resource "random_password" "usr" {
  for_each       = var.users
  length          = 16
  special          = true
  override_special = "/@£$"
}
resource "azuread_user" "usr" {
  for_each             = var.users
  user_principal_name  = each.value.user_principal_name               #(Required) The user principal name (UPN) of the user.
  display_name         = each.value.display_name
  ## other properties redacted

  #Set the users password during creation
  password = random_password.usr[each.key].value
}
resource "azurerm_key_vault" "usr" {
  name           = var.password_vault
  ## other properties redacted
  access_policy { <redacted >  }
  
  #Save a copy of the passwords in the key_vault
  dynamic "secret" {
     for_each = var.users
     content {
        name = secret.user_principal_name
        value = random_password.usr[each.key].value
     }
  }
}
```
Perhaps the scenario of users passwords isn't the best one to think of.. Service Accounts.. anything that needs a key/credential /certificate saving.  We should be able to use a dynamic block!

### Description
When creating a Private Endpoint, a common use case is to create a Private DNS Zone that overrides the Azure PaaS FQDN with the private IP address from the private endpoint. For example, if I have an Azure Storage Account _mystorageaccount_ and I have a Private Endpoint in my VNET, I would create a Private DNS Zone for _blob.core.windows.net_ and create an DNS A-Record for _mystorageaccount_ with the Private Endpoint private IP address.

When I use _azurerm_private_endpoint_ to create the Private Endpoint, the only [exported attribute](https://www.terraform.io/docs/providers/azurerm/r/private_endpoint.html#attributes-reference) is the Resource ID. To find the private IP address of the private endpoint I need to use a _azurerm_private_endpoint_connection_. Here is where I get into problems. The _azurerm_private_endpoint_connection_ is a data reference, so I need to set a dependency on the _azurerm_private_endpoint_ or there will be a runtime failure as the private endpoint has not been created yet, and the data reference is null. 

By setting the dependency between the two, Terraform will not attempt to reference the _azurerm_private_endpoint_connection_ until it is first used, which in the example I have below will not be until after the _azurerm_private_endpoint_ is created. Because Terraform cannot resolve the _azurerm_private_endpoint_connection_ until the execution phase, it means everytime I run this Terraform configuration, the plan phase says it needs to make a change. If I have the private IP address of the private endpoint in a DNS A-Record, it will update that and override the value with the same IP address each time I run _terraform apply_.

Providing the private IP address as an exported attribute in the _azurerm_private_endpoint_ would remove this problem. 

The following example shows how I can retrieve the private IP address of a private-link enabled AKS cluster.
```
# Create a private endpoint to the private AKS cluster
resource "azurerm_private_endpoint" "ple" {
  name                = "kube-apiserver"
  resource_group_name = "test-rg"
  subnet_id           = data.azurerm_subnet.ple_subnet.id

  private_service_connection {
    name                           = "kube-apiserver"
    private_connection_resource_id = azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks.id
    subresource_names              = [ "management" ]
    is_manual_connection           = false
  }
}

# Find the IP Address associated with the private endpoint created above
data "azurerm_private_endpoint_connection" "ple_connection" {
  name                = "kube-apiserver"
  resource_group_name = "test-rg"
  depends_on          = [ azurerm_private_endpoint.ple ]
}

# Create a local variable to the private IP address
locals {
  kube_ple_ip = data.azurerm_private_endpoint_connection.ple_connection.private_service_connection.0.private_ip_address
}

# Create a DNS A-Record using the private IP address
resource "azurerm_private_dns_a_record" "aks_dns_record" {
  name                = "aks-fqdn"
  zone_name           = azurerm_private_dns_zone.build_server_dns_zone.name
  resource_group_name = "test-rg"
  ttl                 = 3600
  records             = [ local.kube_ple_ip ]
}
```

```shell

The issue is silent incorrect behavior: after a successful apply,
the ASG only appears on the IPv4 IP configuration in the Azure Portal,

No debug log is needed to reproduce — the behavior is visible in the
```

### Expected Behaviour

The ASG association should be applied to all IP configurations on the NIC, including IPv6 ones. Azure itself supports ASGs on IPv6 IP configurations — NSG rules referencing ASGs should match traffic on both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

### Actual Behaviour

The ASG is only applied to IPv4 IP configurations. IPv6 IP configurations are skipped entirely. In the Azure Portal, the ASG only appears under the NIC's IPv4 address, not the IPv6 address. NSG rules using ASGs as source/destination therefore do not match IPv6 traffic.

Create an azurerm_network_interface_application_security_group_association
terraform apply

<!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->


### Description

The Azure Storage network rules API does not accept /31 or /32 CIDR prefixes in `ip_rules` — only /0 - /30 are permitted. However, the `azurerm_network_service_tags` data source can 
return /31 CIDRs in its `ipv4_cidrs` output, creating a provider-internal incompatibility: one resource produces values that another resource's validation rejects.
 
Users are forced to write non-trivial `locals` to filter and expand the offending ranges before passing them to `ip_rules`.
 
 The requested improvement is for `azurerm_storage_account` (and `azurerm_storage_account_network_rules`) to automatically filter out /31 and /32 CIDRs from `ip_rules` and expand them 
into their individual host addresses before sending to the Azure API mirroring the behaviour that Azure itself documents as the correct workaround.

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

 * `azurerm_storage_account`, `azurerm_storage_account_network_rules`

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
data "azurerm_network_service_tags" "example" {
   location        = "germanywestcentral"
   service         = "AzureCloud"
   location_filter = "germanywc"
 }
 
 resource "azurerm_storage_account" "example" {
   name                     = "examplestorage"
   resource_group_name      = "example-rg"
   location                 = "switzerlandnorth"
   account_tier             = "Standard"
   account_replication_type = "LRS"
 
   network_rules {
```

```shell
Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply

When applying changes to
module.windows_machine.azurerm_network_interface_security_group_association.main[0],
provider "provider[\"registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm\"]" produced an
```

### Expected Behaviour

`terraform apply` should complete cleanly and the resource should be persisted to state, since the association was actually created successfully in Azure.

### Actual Behaviour

Terraform reports `Provider produced inconsistent result after apply: Root object was present, but now absent`, even though the Network Security Group Association was successfully created.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform apply` to create `azurerm_network_interface_security_group_association`
2. The error surfaces intermittently on the same `apply` that creates the resource

### Important Factoids

This was originally reported as a comment on #32317, which tracks the same class of error (`Provider produced inconsistent result after apply: Root object was present, but now absent`) for a different resource, `azurerm_portal_dashboard`:

> I'm seeing the same issue with Provider version 5.x but it's in a different resource.
>
> ```
> Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply
>
> When applying changes to
> module.windows_machine.azurerm_network_interface_security_group_association.main[0],
> provider "provider[\"registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm\"]" produced an
> unexpected new value: Root object was present, but now absent.
>
> This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's own
> issue tracker.
> ```
>
> — [@kirtigargg, comment on #32317](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/32317#issuecomment-5187950427)

Filing as a separate issue since it's a different resource with a distinct root cause in the code, even though the user-visible error message is identical.

**Suspected root cause**: `resourceNetworkInterfaceSecurityGroupAssociationCreate` in `internal/services/network/network_interface_security_group_association_resource.go` calls `client.CreateOrUpdateCallbackThenPoll(...)` (which polls the Azure long-running-operation status until it reports done), sets the Terraform ID, and then immediately calls `Read`. `Read` does a `Get` on the Network Interface and, if `properties.networkSecurityGroup` is nil, treats the association as removed and clears the resource from state (`d.SetId("")`) - which is exactly what produces "Root object was present, but now absent" from Terraform Core's consistency check.

The Network Interfaces API appears to be eventually consistent in the same way documented for several other resources in this codebase (e.g. `// API has bug, which appears to be eventually consistent` in `internal/services/compute/dedicated_host_resource.go` and `internal/services/network/express_route_circuit_resource.go`): the LRO-completion poller finishing does not guarantee that a subsequent `Get` against a (possibly different, lagging) read path reflects the change yet.

Notably, the sibling resource `azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association` (`internal/services/network/subnet_network_security_group_association_resource.go`) already guards against exactly this by polling the Subnet's (and parent Virtual Network's) `provisioningState` back to `Succeeded` after `CreateOrUpdateCallbackThenPoll` and before calling `Read` - `azurerm_network_interface_security_group_association` has no equivalent wait.

The following diff was generated after upgrading to the recently released v1.34.0:

```
      id:                               "/subscriptions/XXXXX/resourceGroups/XXXXX/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/XXXXX/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/XXXXX" => <computed> (forces new resource)
```

Manually adding `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to the configuration and setting it to `true` also forces a new resource. Setting it to `""` is evaluated as `false`, the default, which also forces a new resource.

```
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = ["skip_service_principal_aad_check"]
  }
```

After the Terraform configuration has been applied, running `terraform apply` should not result in the `azurerm_role_assignment` being recreated since no changes have been made.

`azurerm_role_assignment` gets recreated every subsequent time a `terraform apply` is run because the the `role_definition_id` appears to have changed.

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Are there anything atypical about your accounts that we should know? For example: Running in a Azure China/Germany/Government? --->

We're running in a hub and spoke model of Azure subscriptions where we are adding role definitions to the hub subscription and role assignments to the hub and all spoke subscriptions.

Because `azurerm_role_assignment` effectively doesn't support updates every time a `role_definition_id` changes the resource is destroyed and then re-created.

I believe the issue is with the role assignment client's call to `GetById` which is using the subscription of the provider itself as the scope. ### Expected Behaviour

A (within reason) `terraform import` should result in no changes.

### Actual Behaviour

`parallelism` & `size` force replacement:

```
  # azurerm_storage_blob.resource must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "resource" {
      ~ access_tier            = "Hot" -> (known after apply)
      ~ id                     = "https://bucket.blob.core.windows.net/container/blob.json" -> (known after apply)
      ~ metadata               = {} -> (known after apply)
        name                   = "blob.json"
      + parallelism            = 8 # forces replacement
      + size                   = 0 # forces replacement
      + source_content         = jsonencode(
            {
              + thing   = "https://example.com"
              + thing2 = "https://example.com/more-stuff"
            } # forces replacement
        )
      ~ url                    = "https://bucket.blob.core.windows.net/container/blob.json" -> (known after apply)
        # (4 unchanged attributes hidden)

      - timeouts {}
    }
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform import ${a blob} …`
2. `terraform plan`

### Important Factoids

You can, if you know what you are doing, do the following:
1. `terraform state pull`
2. Find the resource in the state file; `parallelism` & `size` will be present, and incorrect. Adjust their values to match what your `.tf` file has, to remove the difference.
3. Bump the state file serial.
4. `terraform state push` 

But for obvious reasons, you must know what you're doing here, and be careful! (Backup your state file first.)

This doesn't alleviate the `source_content` delta, which is also forcing replacement. You _can_ also eliminate that using the same method as above: manually modify the state file to set `source_content`, if that applies to your case. (Here, it did, as that is how I'm getting the blob's content.) TF stores the literal content in the state file — i.e., the exact value that `source_content` computes to. So, in this example, I adjust `source_content` to the _result_ of that `jsonencode` call, and then there's no delta. You must be _precise_: JSON has a lot of `"`s, which must be escaped (`source_content` in the state file is a string, which is the type of the result of `jsonencode`), and you must get the spacing right (there is none, i.e., the JSON is compact) and you must get the order right (the same order plan shows seems to work, and I presume TF must be generating a canonical JSON somehow).

This appears to be the line in the parser which is missing at least one additional item that should pass the check. 

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/6e58aae8316eac0a836fafc61a6ec2ad6a8adebf/internal/services/authorization/parse/role_definition.go#L54


In the Terraform Plan error, we get:

Error: expect scope to start with one of /subscriptions/, /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/, got "/providers/Microsoft.Subscription/aliases/sub-alias"

We need to add /providers/Microsoft.Subscription/aliases as a passing pattern to this validator to allow us to create custom roles that can be assigned here.   

In order to grant the required permissions to run a plan locally when managing subscription aliases, the "Microsoft.Subscription/aliases/write" permission is required to be assigned to the users running the plan. 

Assigning this permission via CLI works fine, just fails with Terraform.

### Description

**Background**
When deploying a Storage Account from an agent that is behind a corporate firewall that is prohibited access to `*.blob.core.windows.net` and `*.queue.core.windows.net`, the deployment will fail. 

After taking 5 minutes trying to connect to mystorage.queue.core.windows.net the deployment fails with error: 
`Error: reading queue properties for AzureRM Storage Account "mystorage": queues.Client#GetServiceProperties: Failure sending request: StatusCode=0 -- Original Error: context deadline exceeded`

This is initiated by #16240, and related to #2977 and #9314, but different as it's about a corporate firewall. When this firewall is temporarily allowed access to `*.blob.core.windows.net` and `*.queue.core.windows.net`, it can continue to deploy the Storage Account, next it can deploy a Private Endpoint, and after a sleep of 2 minutes (yes, ugly hack) it can create containers. 

But as many large corporate enterprises, the security team has established it's a data-exfiltration risk to allow access to `*.blob.core.windows.net` and `*.queue.core.windows.net`, and therefor the corporate firewall will block access. This request is from a large Dutch enterprise building semiconductor machines.

**Request**
Add an option to not-access the data-plane (to fetch the queue properties). Perhaps because of this the functionality of azurerm_storage_account will be slightly limited, but at least it's possible to deploy and update a Storage Account using the control-plane from behind a corporate firewall.

Perhaps this can be done by specifying an additional property on the azurerm_storage_account resource like `do_not_access_data_plane`, or by setting a flag in the `azurerm` provider features section.

Optional we could try to make this change ourselves, but would love to get advice upfront. We're not skilled enough yet, but we can give it a try.

```hcl
  do_not_access_data_plane = true
}

or

provider "azurerm" {
  features {
    storage_account {
      do_not_access_data_plane = true
    }
  }
}
```

### Description

Right now only absolute paths are allowed for `source`. This is inconsistant with most other file based functions. 

Requiring the property to be used with absolute paths produces inconsistant applys, if plan and apply phases are not executed from the _same directory_. 

A similar example of this behavior is outlined [in a closed github issue](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/7613) for terraform (different users executing plan and apply).
A more up to date example are pipelines, where the plan and apply phases may be executed in different stages (and on different agents, e.g. in Azure DevOps). We use different stages, because we need an approval step after the plan (this seems a natural setup). 
If the apply phase is now executed on a server having a different folder structure, the apply throws the following error:
```
│ Error: Provider produced inconsistent final plan
│ 
│ When expanding the plan for
│ azurerm_storage_blob.website to
│ include new values learned so far during apply, provider
│ "registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm" produced an invalid new value for
│ .source: was
│ cty.StringVal("/home/vsts/work/1/s/app.zip"),
│ but now
│ cty.StringVal("/home/[private folder name]/work/1/s/app.zip").
│ 
│ This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's
│ own issue tracker.
```
I'm aware that the core problem is the changing path, not the provider. But as these are typical scenarios handled correctly in terraform itself and many other providers, so it would be nice if `azurerm_storage_blob` could be enabled to read files from relative paths too.

I wouldn't expect to be any risk of regressions through that enhancement, as relative paths right now throw an immediate error (tested with `${path.module}/app.zip`
```
│ Error: creating Blob "app.zip" (Container "x" / Account "y"): opening: open ./app.zip: no such file or directory
```

* azurerm_storage_blob

```hcl
resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "website" {
  name                   = "app.zip"
  storage_account_name   = "account"
  storage_container_name = "container"
  content_md5            = data.archive_file.source.output_md5
  type                   = "Block"
  source                 = "${path.module}/app.zip"
```

After a certificate that is managed in state with `azurerm_key_vault_certificate is renewed by Acmebot, terraform plan should show the changed values for the key vault certificate

### Actual Behaviour

Terraform crashes with panic output

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Add an ACME issued certificate to key vault with azurerm_key_vault_certificate and terraform apply
2. Renew the certificate via Acmebot azure function (https://github.com/shibayan/keyvault-acmebot). This will set the certificate policy subject to empty.
3. terraform plan

### Important Factoids

This is the same issue that was fixed in azurerm 2.22.0 for data.azurerm_key_vault_certificate but still exists in the azurerm_key_vault_certificate resource (https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/8019). 

Since the subject is empty after the certificate is renewed, the terraform throws a nil pointer exception when loading the state here: https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/87318246fb202c6405fb1f68759960bd67b51dae/azurerm/internal/services/keyvault/key_vault_certificate_resource.go#L833

When certificate is created but in a `failed` state, the created certificate should be tracked in Terraform state.

 Alternately, the module could attempt to delete the resources it created so it matches state, but purge-protection key vault policies might make this hard to guarantee state matches.

### Actual Behaviour

When certificate is created in a `failed` state, the `apply` command fails and Terraform state is not updated. During the next `plan`, Terraform will plan to create a new certificate, and fail during `apply` when an existing certificate is still provisioned.

The `privateLinkServiceConnectionState` object should be included as a read-only attribute. See the [Azure API documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/virtualnetwork/private-endpoints/get?view=rest-virtualnetwork-2024-07-01&tabs=HTTP#get-private-endpoint-with-manual-approval-connection). This is IMO important to reflect back, since it shows whether the associated [Private Endpoint Connection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/virtualnetwork/private-link-services/get-private-endpoint-connection?view=rest-virtualnetwork-2024-07-01&tabs=HTTP) is `Pending`, `Approved` or `Disconnected`.

Note: Depending on whether it's a manual or automatic service connection it can exist under different places:

- `manualPrivateLinkServiceConnections[].privateLinkServiceConnectionState`
- `privateLinkServiceConnections[].privateLinkServiceConnectionState`

So we need to get it from different places depending on the `is_manual_connection` boolean.

* `azurerm_route_table` can take a route as a list of `route` objects
    * Notes on 3.x of the azurerm provider say it now takes a set - I tried that as well, and have the same error
    * [Docs](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/3.109.0/docs/resources/route_table#route) may need to be updated to indicate it takes a set

### Description
I frequently have a need to create a VNET link between a VNET in one subscription and a Private DNS Zone in a different subscription using the azurerm provider.
Simultaneously it is also required to allow the configuration to be dynamic such that this code could be put into a module and provided the necessary context information via configuration variables to create the needed linkages.

Currently, this appears not to be possible as far as I can tell;  Right now the `private_dns_zone_name` argument is how one indicates which Private DNS Zone to create the link with, but there is no way to provide the subscription context dynamically.

I thought about specifying a different provider with an alias in order to provide the context of the private DNS zone but this appears to be problematic because we can't set providers dynamically, as I would need to in the case of a completely configuration-driven approach.  The approach of setting a different provider for the `azurerm_private_dns_zone_virtual_network_link` is what was suggested in the referenced Github issue below.  Unfortunately that approach doesn't work for my scenario.

### New or Affected Resource(s)
* azurerm_private_dns_zone_virtual_network_link

### Potential Terraform Configuration
I would like to propose that , similar to the way that the VNET context is provided using a full resource ID in the `virtual_network_id` , the same should be possible for the Private DNS Zone.  
In order to provide some backward compatibility in the short term, perhaps two attributes can be supported:
1) The `private_dns_zone_name`.  If used, behaviour would be as it is today - no change;
2) A new attribute in which one may provide the full resource ID of the Private DNS Zone.   I would propose the name `private_dns_zone_id`.  If used, the Private DNS Zone would be looked up using the full resource ID from whichever subscription it happens to be in

If both arguments above are used simultaneously, I think an error should be raised informing the user they should only use one of them.  Perhaps at some point in the future, the original argument would become deprecated.

Potential new syntax:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_resource_group" "example" {
  name     = "example-resources"
  location = "West Europe"
}

resource "azurerm_private_dns_zone" "example" {
  name                = "mydomain.com"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
}

resource "azurerm_private_dns_zone_virtual_network_link" "example" {
  name                  = "test"
  resource_group_name   = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  private_dns_zone_id = azurerm_private_dns_zone.example.id
  virtual_network_id    = azurerm_virtual_network.example.id
}
```

### Description

Configuring 

```terraform
  sas_policy {
    expiration_period = "00.01:00:00"
    expiration_action = "Block"
  }
```
leads to error:

```terraform
Error: expected sas_policy.0.expiration_action to be one of ["Log"], got Block
```

[Terraform docs say](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_account#expiration_action-4):

```markdown
[expiration_action](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_account#expiration_action-4) - (Optional) The SAS expiration action. The only possible value is Log at this moment. Defaults to Log.
```

```text
The SAS Expiration Action defines the action to be performed when sasPolicy.sasExpirationPeriod is violated. The 'Log' action can be used for audit purposes and the 'Block' action can be used to block and deny the usage of SAS tokens that do not adhere to the sas policy expiration period.
```

<!---

### Panic Output

<!--- If Terraform produced a panic, please provide a link to a GitHub Gist containing the output of the `crash.log`. --->

### Expected Behaviour

<!--- What should have happened? --->
Terraform should destroy access policies.

### Actual Behaviour

<!--- What actually happened? --->
Terraform created a key vault.
Terraform created an access policy for the key vault.
The Terraform configuration for the key vault was updated (uncomment `enabled_for_disk_encryption`) which caused Terraform to update the access policy permission casing to title-case.
The access policies must exactly match what Azure returns in the Azure REST API, but Terraform has updated the casing of the permissions which differs from the initial creation Terraform had performed (lowercase).

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Please list the steps required to reproduce the issue. --->

1. az ad sp create-for-rbac
2. Set a TF_VAR for `service_principal_id` with the appId from the previous step.
2. `terraform apply`
3. `terraform state show azurerm_key_vault.kv` observe the absence of the access policy.
4. `terraform state show azurerm_key_vault_access_policy.ap` observe the lower-case casing of the access policy permissions.
2. Uncomment the property `enabled_for_disk_encryption` on the key vault.
2. `terraform apply`
3. `terraform state show azurerm_key_vault.kv` observe the appearance of the access policy
4. `terraform state show azurerm_key_vault_access_policy.ap` observe the title-case casing of the access policy permissions.
5. `terraform destroy` observe the destroy will never finish and hang until timeout for the access policy.

### Important Factoids

<!--- Are there anything atypical about your accounts that we should know? For example: Running in a Azure China/Germany/Government? --->

When a Key Vault is updated through Terraform, the casing of the access policy permissions in Terraform state is made to be title-case, but the casing of the access policy permissions in Azure itself remain what they were initially created as.

When a Key Vault is updated through the Azure Portal, the casing of the access policy permissions is made to be title-case.

`Read` sets `notification_settings` from the API response, so when the service omits the property the provider records an empty value and the next plan wants to add it back.

### Steps to Reproduce

The service accepts the property and then discards it. Reproduced with Terraform out of the picture by sending the request directly to ARM.

`PUT .../providers/Microsoft.DevTestLab/schedules/shutdown-computevm-<vm>?api-version=2018-09-15` with the property spelled exactly as the specification documents it:

```json
"notificationSettings": {
  "status": "Enabled",
  "timeInMinutes": 15,
  "emailRecipient": "a@example.com",
  "webhookUrl": "https://example-webhook-url.example.com"
}
```

The response reports `"provisioningState": "Succeeded"` with no validation error, and echoes back:

```json
"notificationSettings": {
  "emailRecipient": "a@example.com",
  "status": "Enabled",
  "timeInMinutes": 15
}
```

A follow-up `GET` agrees. Reproduced on api-versions `2018-09-15` and `2016-05-15`. The casings `webHookUrl`, `WebhookUrl` and `webhookURL` were also tried, and all are discarded, so this is not a casing mismatch.

The property is still published: `models.tsp` in `azure-rest-api-specs` declares `webhookUrl?: string` with the description "The webhook URL to which the notification will be sent", and the `Schedules_Get` example response includes it.

### Important Factoids

This is a recent change. A CI suite that has set this property since April 2025 passed consistently until 26 August 2026 and has failed on every run since, on an unchanged provider version and unchanged configuration.

Silently accepting and discarding the value is the awkward part. A validation error would surface the problem immediately, whereas today it only appears as an unresolvable diff.

### Description

When Azure role assignment conditions are used, principal_type becomes a required field when performing a role assignment rather than optional (ref: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/31635)

It is a somewhat common pattern to do this:
```hcl
data "azurerm_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azurerm_role_assignment" "executor_secrets_officer_kv" {
  scope                = module.fnl_keyvault.keyvault_id
  role_definition_name = "Key Vault Secrets Officer"
  principal_id         = data.azurerm_client_config.current.object_id
  principal_type       = "ServicePrincipal"
}
```
Without including principal_type, this block will execute successfully whether run locally by a user or whether run in CICD as a service_principal. Once principal_type is required, we now need to either run a mock provisioner block checking the principal_type from Az cli, env variable, etc OR add a new variable for the principal_type of the current account running terraform operations.

This could be avoided if principal_type was added to the data source azurerm_client_config.

4. Import existing virtual machine as an `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine` with `terraform import ...`
5. Run `terraform plan`
6. Observe plan wants to destroy/recreate vm

### Expected Behaviour

There is no setting mentioned in the `azurerm_storage_account` documentation for disabling public access to blob storage, nor anything else that mentions blob storage public access control.  

### Actual Behaviour

Since our Azure Policy requires blob storage public access to be false, the resource as created above fails to pass policy and does not deploy.  

Some googling pointed at [a StackOverflow discussion](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73741756/disabling-allow-public-blob-access-using-terraform) where from 3.0 onwards, the `allow_blob_public_access` argument was changed to `allow_nested_items_to_be_public`.  This does not make any sense from an Azure storage perspective - we refer to blobs as blobs or blob containers, not as nested items.  

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Assign Azure Policy using the built-in definition "[Preview]: Storage account public access should be disallowed" to a subscription or resource group scope
2. Wait about 30 minutes for the policy to take effect
3. Create a main.tf using the above storage account example in the resource group scope defined in step 1
4. Run `terraform apply` - it will be denied by the policy
5. Edit the main.tf from step 3 to include allow_nested_items_to_be_public = false
6. Save main.tf and run `terraform apply` - it will pass the policy validation

### Description

We are using terraform with a custom module "custom-acme-registration-route53" to handle requesting SSL certificates from Let's Encrypt using DNS Zones stored in AWS Route53. After getting the certificate the goal is adding it to an Azure Key Vault to be consumed by application gateway and be rotated automatically upon certificate renewal. Unfortunately, terraform can't create new versions of certificates in Azure key vaults and the vault in question has soft delete and purge protection enabled so Terraform fails trying to delete and purge the certificate entry to recreate it afterwards. In order to achieve the aim we plan to grab output of the custom module that contains the certificate contents in p12 format and store it in Azure blob storage using the "azurerm_storage_blob" terraform module. Currently this module does not have a password argument and without the password the certificate can't be imported to Key Vault as azure gives the following error message:     
```
    + CategoryInfo          : CloseError: (:) [Import-AzKeyVaultCertificate], CryptographicException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : Microsoft.Azure.Commands.KeyVault.ImportAzureKeyVaultCertificate
```
Please see details here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56028786/import-azkeyvaultcertificate-cmdlet-results-in-key-not-valid-for-user-in-specif

Please look into adding password argument to the contents of the blob being saved so that the resulting certificate file could be used for key vault import.

**In the meantime, is there a way I could work around the issue? I've tried adding the password as blob metadata but that had no impact on the import process.**

### Description

Currently, the AzureRM Terraform provider does not expose the dedicated_backend_connection property within the backend_http_settings block of the azurerm_application_gateway resource. This setting is critical for scenarios requiring persistent backend connections—such as Windows Authentication in mid-tier services—where load balancing across multiple backend nodes can disrupt session continuity.

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_application_gateway

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
Enabling this setting has been shown to resolve authentication issues in environments where multiple backend nodes are used. Without it, Application Gateway may reuse idle connections, breaking session affinity for services that rely on stateful authentication mechanisms.

Please add native support for the dedicated_backend_connection property in the azurerm_application_gateway resource to enable full configuration via Terraform.

backend_http_settings {
    name                                = "setting"
    cookie_based_affinity               = "Disabled"
    port                                = 443
    probe_name                          = "setting"
    protocol                            = "Https"
    request_timeout                     = 30
    dedicated_backend_connection        = $true
    pick_host_name_from_backend_address = true
    
    connection_draining {
      enabled            = true
      drain_timeout_sec  = 60
    }
  }
```

After a failed attempt to update the certificate, the changed value should not be persistet in state and therefore tried to update on the next `apply`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform apply`
2. Note the current thumbprint
  1. Go to Azure Portal and open the created certificate
  2. Note the Thumbprint to check if certificate was updated later
4. Create a Pending Certificate Operation by  1. Go to the Azure Portal, open the created keyvault  2. open the created secret
  3. Click on `New Version`
  4. Make sure `Generate`is selected and go ahead
  5. A blue information should inform you about a pending certificate and can be viewed at `Certificate Operation`
6. Change `input` of `terraform_data` to generate new certificate
7. Run `terraform apply`
8. Receive Conflict Error
9. Run `terraform apply` again -> No changes
10. Check if certificate was updated in keyvault
  1. Open Certificate in Portal
  2. Check if Thumbprint is changed
  4. It isn't :(

Even when we resolve the pending operation by removing it, the resource still thinks everything is fine and never updates.

### Expected Behavior

Earlier version of azurerm <= 2.15 created an API with subscription_required = true by default which makes all the APIs secure.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28331812/88827847-5e0d1e00-d1c2-11ea-8095-bb39c8136598.png)

### Actual Behavior

AzureRm now creates API with subscription_required = false by default, making all apis that were previously secure suddenly public. Also this is not the same experience when API is created manually through portal which also have checkbox selected by default for subscription required. Those who have not pinned the azurerm version may accidentally release a public API in production. Better to set the default as true and secure and allow users to override it by setting it to false when a public API is required

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28331812/88828840-ae38b000-d1c3-11ea-96a6-ab2b1813aeab.png)

**Terraform (and AzureRM Provider) Version**

- TF 0.11.14
- AzureRM 1.33.0

**Affected Resource(s)**

- azurerm_api_management

**Terraform Configuration**

```
resource "azurerm_api_management" "apim" {
  name                = "${var.name}"
  location            = "${var.location}"
  resource_group_name = "${var.rg_name}"

  sku = ["${var.sku}"]

  additional_location {
    location = "brazilsouth"
  }
  additional_location {
    location = "eastus2"
  }
  additional_location {
    location = "southeastasia"
  }

  [...]

  tags = "${var.tags}"
}
```

**Expected Behavior**

Enable several additional_location on the Apim resource

**Actual Behavior**

"Error: module.api_management.azurerm_api_management.apim: additional_location: attribute supports 1 item maximum, config has 3 declared"

On the Terraform documentation we can find that additional_location can be one or more blocks : 
> additional_location - One or more additional_location blocks as documented below.

By searching in the code, I found this : 

https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/master/azurerm/resource_arm_api_management.go#L123

```
"additional_location": {
                Type:     schema.TypeList,
                Optional: true,
                MaxItems: 1,
[...]
}
```

This MaxItems variable should be removed to handle multiple additional_location I think.

### Description

The recently merged PR #30204 added support for the arguments
resilient_vm_creation_enabled and resilient_vm_deletion_enabled to the
azurerm_virtual_machine_scale_set resource.

However, the same capability was not added to the
azurerm_orchestrated_virtual_machine_scale_set resource, even though both VMSS resource types support these resiliency features in Azure.

This request is for the provider to expose these arguments in
azurerm_orchestrated_virtual_machine_scale_set as well, enabling parity between the two VMSS resource types and giving users access to Azure’s resilient VM lifecycle management in orchestrated (Flex) scale sets.

### Expected Behaviour

Our Terraform configuration has been working without errors for a year, and we have not made any changes to the containers. Terraform should run and output "No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration."

### Actual Behaviour

In the last week the issue has occurred 4 times on different environments at random times among around 40 deployments to different environments. During deploy container entries in the state file are suddenly deleted. Terraform then tries to create resources that are not in the state and fails with an error when it encounters them in Azure.
It was mitigated by importing the container resources. On one environment it reproduced even after the import. Any external or human interference is excluded. The deployment is exclusively run from Azure DevOps pipelines.

### Steps to Reproduce

terraform plan
or
terraform apply

The issue is transient. I cannot reproduce it by just redeploying. It happens randomly. No patterns have been observed.
