### Description

Currently the global API Policy for API management is configured with the `policy` block of the  `azurerm_api_management` resource. However this makes it impossible to apply any policy that includes references to the same API management instance or things contained within it, because you create a circular dependency. 

I propose a new resource for the global policy, much like the seperate resources for the policy at API, Product and Operation levels.

For example, I want to deploy API management, a logger config using `azurerm_api_management_logger` (which depends on api managment being deployed already) and thren global policy to log all requests to that logger - I can't because the policy is part of the `azurerm_api_management` resource which has to deploy before `azurerm_api_management_logger` can, and I need the logger deployed before I can apply the global policy containing `<log-to-eventhub logger-id="${eventhub_logger_id}">` otherwise it is rejected by API Management.

Another example - in the global policy I want to IP whitelist requests into API Management from itself. I cannot because the IP address I need to put as an input in the policy is an output of itself.

### New or Affected Resource(s)

* Deprecate policy block on `azurerm_api_management`
* Add new resource `azurerm_api_management_policy`

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
resource "azurerm_api_management_policy" "my_global_policy" {
  api_management_name = "abc"
  resource_group_name = "abc"
  xml_content   = "....policy xml goes here ... "
}
```

### Description

Currently, `storage_data_disk` is not an attribute that `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine` or `azurerm_windows_virtual_machine` supports and we are forced to use a secondary `azurerm_managed_disk` and `azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment`. While on the surface, this doesn't seem like a big deal, in some cases this can cause problems.

Issues with not being able to use a `storage_data_disk` in an `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine` specifically:

- If using a `cloud-init`/`user_data`/`custom_data` script that mounts a disk to a specific location, it's very likely that the disk won't actually be created or attached when the script runs in the VM. Therefore the script fails.
- In line with above, if we are creating a VM from a custom image that requires either a snapshotted data disk to exist to be mounted at a specific location, that's not possible either at the moment (or it will cause a bunch of errors in the VM when it boots up, presuming the disk mounts to the right spot in the end).

As it stands, if we want to leverage that kind of functionality, we have to revert to using the (soon to be deprecated) `azurerm_virtual_machine` resource.

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

`azurerm_linux_virtual_machine`, `azurerm_windows_virtual_machine`

### Description

Currently the azure_virtual_machine_extension resource requires to specify the concerned VM with the parameter "virtual_machine_name". This is not consistent with other resources that require the "virtual_machine_id" parameter. Also, I think that it would be safer to use the id instead of the name.

```hcl

  subscription_name = "example"

}

  principal_id         = "valid principal id"
  role_definition_name = "owner"
  scope                = azurerm_subscription.example.id # /providers/Microsoft.Subscription/aliases/xxxx-xxxx-xxxx
```

### Expected Behaviour

A role assignment is created with the respective properties.

`azurerm_role_assignment` fails to parse the `scope` with a resource id for a subscription alias. Throws error and exits Terraform.

1. Attempt to create a role assignment to the new alias created by Terraform.

* **App Service `win32_status` property** - Due to a change made in the service to the underlying type of the Auto Heal property `win32_status` combined with a prior bug (in `v3.62.1` and earlier) causing the value of this property to be stored incorrectly in state as an empty string, the value of this property could not be updated or state migrated to accommodate the necessary type change in the state. <!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->


### Description

Scenario:

A linux virtual machine with an attached managed disk has an attribute change requiring replacement of the virtual machine resource. The azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment has a dependency on the azurerm_linux_virtual_machine by way of the virtual_machine_id, and so will also be replaced.

The natural order for Terraform:

1. destroy azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment
2. destroy azurerm_linux_virtual_machine
3. create azurerm_linux_virtual_machine
4. create azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment

The problem here is that the VM will experience a very non-graceful removal of the managed disk. Ideally, the virtual machine shutdown would happen before the disk is detached, allowing services writing to the disk to stop gracefully, and then the file system to be gracefully unmounted before device is removed.

aws_volume_attachment addresses this same problem with either of two options:

> [skip_destroy](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/volume_attachment#skip_destroy-1) - (Optional, Boolean) Set this to true if you do not wish to detach the volume from the instance to which it is attached at destroy time, and instead just remove the attachment from Terraform state. This is useful when destroying an instance which has volumes created by some other means attached.

> [stop_instance_before_detaching](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs/resources/volume_attachment#stop_instance_before_detaching-1) - (Optional, Boolean) Set this to true to ensure that the target instance is stopped before trying to detach the volume. Stops the instance, if it is not already stopped.

Either or both of these options would solve the issue.

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
resource "azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment" "example" {
  managed_disk_id    = azurerm_managed_disk.example.id
  virtual_machine_id = azurerm_virtual_machine.example.id
  lun                = "10"
  caching            = "ReadWrite"
  skip_destroy       = true
}

or

resource "azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment" "example" {
  managed_disk_id    = azurerm_managed_disk.example.id
  virtual_machine_id = azurerm_virtual_machine.example.id
  lun                = "10"
  caching            = "ReadWrite"
  stop_vm_before_detaching       = true
}
```

### Description

According to enterprise scale set design by Microsoft, exists 2 policies that are part of best practices and prevent creation of subnets without nsg, subnets without route tables:
https://www.azadvertizer.net/azpolicyadvertizer/Deny-Subnet-Without-Nsg.html
https://www.azadvertizer.net/azpolicyadvertizer/Deny-Subnet-Without-Udr.html
When these policies applied, it impossible to create/modify subnet in terraform cause "subnet_network_security_group_association" and "subnet_route_table_association" are separate resources, that require subnet to be created. So "azurerm_subnet" cannot do same as can be done in az cli, az powershell, ARM Templates and bicep - create resource with association to nsg and route table via 1 step.

### Description

Azure Monitor native OTLP ingestion requires a Data Collection Rule whose stable ARM representation includes `properties.directDataSources.otelMetrics`. Each entry identifies a direct OTLP metrics source by `name` and `streams`.

`azurerm_monitor_data_collection_rule` in AzureRM 4.78.0 has no schema for `directDataSources`, so a DCR for direct OpenTelemetry Collector ingestion cannot be fully represented by the AzureRM provider. Users must instead manage the entire DCR with `azapi_resource` or an ARM deployment. Patching an AzureRM-managed DCR from a second resource would create overlapping ownership and drift risk.

Please add first-class HCL support for the stable ARM `directDataSources` property, including `otelMetrics`. Support for the corresponding direct OTLP logs and traces fields could follow the same ARM shape.

The Azure Verified Module for this resource currently implements the DCR with `azapi_resource` and exposes typed `direct_data_sources` input, which is useful prior art but does not remove the AzureRM resource coverage gap.

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

`azurerm_monitor_data_collection_rule`

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
resource "azurerm_monitor_data_collection_rule" "example" {
  name                        = "example"
  resource_group_name         = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location                    = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  data_collection_endpoint_id = azurerm_monitor_data_collection_endpoint.example.id

  direct_data_sources {
    otel_metrics {
      name    = "otel-metrics"
      streams = ["Custom-Metrics-Otel"]
    }
  }

  destinations {
    monitor_account {
      monitor_account_id = azurerm_monitor_workspace.example.id
      name               = "metrics"
    }
  }

  data_flow {
    streams      = ["Custom-Metrics-Otel"]
    destinations = ["metrics"]
  }
}
```

The exact HCL naming is illustrative; the important requirement is full ownership of ARM `properties.directDataSources.otelMetrics` by this resource.

<!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->


### Description

## Summary

Azure Storage [Geo Priority Replication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-redundancy-priority-replication) is a Generally Available feature (GA since November 2025) that prioritizes blob replication for storage accounts using **GRS** or **GZRS** redundancy.

When enabled, it provides an SLA guaranteeing that the **Last Sync Time (LST)** for Block Blob data remains lagged **15 minutes or less** for 99% of the billing month — significantly improving the RPO for disaster recovery scenarios.

## Current Behavior

The `azurerm_storage_account` resource does not expose the `geoPriorityReplicationStatus` API property, making it impossible to enable or manage Geo Priority Replication via Terraform.

## Desired Behavior

Add a new argument `geo_priority_replication_enabled` (bool) to `azurerm_storage_account` to allow enabling/disabling this feature. This argument should only be valid when `account_replication_type` is `GRS` or `GZRS`.

## Notes

- Billing for this feature began January 1, 2026
- SLA covers Block Blobs only (Page Blobs and Append Blobs are excluded)
- Maps to the `geoPriorityReplicationStatus` property in the Azure Storage API

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_storage_account

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
resource "azurerm_resource_group" "example" {
  name     = "example-resources"
  location = "East US"
}

resource "azurerm_storage_account" "example" {
  name                     = "examplestoracc"
  resource_group_name      = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location                 = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  account_tier             = "Standard"
  account_replication_type = "GRS"

  # New argument to be added
  geo_priority_replication_enabled = true
}
```

```
  name     = "imported-cert"
  key_vault_id = "XXXXXXX"

  certificate {

    password = ""

  certificate_policy {

      name = "Self"
    }

    key_properties {
      exportable = true
      key_size   = 2048
      key_type   = "RSA"
      reuse_key  = false
    }

    secret_properties {
      content_type = "application/x-pkcs12"
    }
  }
}
```

### Expected Behaviour

azurerm_api_management_api should be replaced as shown in `terraform plan` without any error. 

### Actual Behaviour

The first time running `terraform apply` always fails with 'A resource with the ID ... already exist...'. The second time running `terraform apply` works then and completes the needed changes. But in a CI/CD pipeline this always leads to a broken pipeline and needs retries. 

The reason for that is similar to the reason of https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/23322 where azurerm does not follow correctly the polling URL of the Azure API where a long running operation should be tracked. Instead azurerm zu goes ahead and tries to create the api again (with the new setting) but then it finds the previous API for which the delete operation has not finished yet.

Here it is clearly visible that the DELETE Call was made to the Azure API and then immediately after that the certation starts which find then API which is going to be deleted. It can identified by the "displayName" of the API which contains still "single version" which is the API which must be deleted. I added the string to the "displayName" by intent so that it can be tracked which version of the api is the one which actually triggers the conflict.

As you can see in the documentation of the Azure API the DELETE resource normally response with "202" and URLs where the actual progress can be tracked: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/apimanagement/apis/delete?view=rest-apimanagement-2024-05-01&tabs=HTTP#apimanagementdeleteapi
But this response seems to be ignored by azurem. So, it similar to what happens in https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/23322 for which PR with a fix is still pending: https://github.com/hashicorp/go-azure-sdk/pull/1090. So maybe this would also be fixed when the PR is merged. But I am not sure. @wuxu92 Can please confirm/verify that?



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Apply the above configuration with `local.additional_version=false`

### Description

request_body_enforcement is only supported in azurerm_web_application_firewall_policy, it is not supported in azurerm_application_gateway waf_configuration.

A terraform plan/apply will revert this to default setting:

~ policy_settings {
  ~  request_body_enforce =     false -> true
   }

This should be supported in both waf_configuration and web_application_firewall_policy.

This is a regression introduced with #21129 where the `firewall_policy_id` of `http_listener` blocks and `azurerm_application_gateway` itself is attempted to be validated as `Microsoft.Network/firewallPolicies` when it should be validated as `Microsoft.Network/ApplicationGatewayWebApplicationFirewallPolicies`.

Change [L20 of terraform-provider-azurerm/internal/services/network
/application_gateway_resource.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v3.50.0/internal/services/network/application_gateway_resource.go#L20) from:
```golang
firewallValidate "github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/internal/services/firewall/validate"
```

to
```golang
firewallValidate "github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/internal/services/network/validate"
```

Then change `ValidateFunc` on [L543](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v3.50.0/internal/services/network/application_gateway_resource.go#L543) and [L1507](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v3.50.0/internal/services/network/application_gateway_resource.go#L1507) to use `firewallValidate.ApplicationGatewayWebApplicationFirewallPolicyID` instead of `firewallValidate.FirewallPolicyID`.

### Actual Behaviour

To test my implementation, I fixed the min_days_remaining property of the acme_certificate resource to 1. The idea behind this is that I don't have to wait a certain number of days to test automatic renewal, I just have to wait for tomorrow. The first time I launch my pipeline, it will create the certificate and push it to my key vault.
- The second time : the behaviour is OK, like in the "Expected Behaviour" block. A new certificate is generated and push to my key vault as the current version. The old one becomes the old version.
- The third time : it is the time when the bug appear, it seems that is considered that I want to change the reuse_key from false to true (Already fixed to true in the code) and it forces the replacement of the resource. After, if I check my certificate, there is nothing in the old versions section, and there is a brand new certificate in the current version section.
- The 4th time : the behaviour is OK...
- The 5th time : the behaviour is KO...
- and so on

### AzureRM Provider Version

4.20.0

### Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

`azurerm_storage_blob`, `azurerm_storage_container`

### Terraform Configuration Files

#### Step 1

Original state, referencing storage account via deprecated parameter `storage_account_name`, works fine:

```hcl
resource "azurerm_resource_group" "this" {
  name     = "reproduce-storage-blob-bug"
  location = "norwayeast"
}

resource "azurerm_storage_account" "this" {
  name                     = "reproducestorageblobbug"
  resource_group_name      = azurerm_resource_group.this.name
  location                 = azurerm_resource_group.this.location
  account_replication_type = "LRS"
  account_tier             = "Standard"
}

resource "azurerm_storage_container" "this" {
  name                 = "reproduce-storage-blob-account-reference-bug"
  storage_account_name = azurerm_storage_account.this.name
}

resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this" {
  name                   = "foo.txt"
  storage_account_name   = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_name # this storage account reference via the storage container is significant
  storage_container_name = azurerm_storage_container.this.name
  type                   = "Block"
  content_type           = "text/plain"
  source_content         = "bar"
}
```

but it produces warnings

```
Warning: Argument is deprecated

  with azurerm_storage_container.this,
  on main.tf line 16, in resource "azurerm_storage_container" "this":
  16:   storage_account_name = azurerm_storage_account.this.name

the `storage_account_name` property has been deprecated in favour of
`storage_account_id` and will be removed in version 5.0 of the Provider.

Warning: Deprecated attribute

  on main.tf line 22, in resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this":
  22:   storage_account_name   = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_name

The attribute "storage_account_name" is deprecated. Refer to the provider
documentation for details.

(and one more similar warning elsewhere)
```

### Debug Output/Panic Output

#### Step 2

Attempting to fix the warnings by updating both the `azurerm_storage_blob` and `azurerm_storage_container` resources to reference the storage account via ID instead of name:

```diff
 resource "azurerm_storage_container" "this" {
   name               = "reproduce-storage-blob-account-reference-bug"
-  storage_account_name = azurerm_storage_account.this.name
+  storage_account_id = azurerm_storage_account.this.id
 }

 resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this" {
   name                   = "foo.txt"
-  storage_account_name   = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_name
+  storage_account_id     = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_id
   storage_container_name = azurerm_storage_container.this.name
   type                   = "Block"
```

This fails `terraform validate`, because contrary to what the second warning implies, the `azurerm_storage_blob` does _not_ (yet) accept `storage_account_id` as a parameter:

```
Error: Missing required argument

  on main.tf line 21, in resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this":
  21: resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this" {

The argument "storage_account_name" is required, but no definition was found.

Error: Unsupported argument

  on main.tf line 23, in resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this":
  23:   storage_account_id     = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_id

An argument named "storage_account_id" is not expected here.
```

#### Step 3

Attempting to fix at least the first warning, by updating _only_ the `azurerm_storage_container` (but not the `azurerm_storage_blob`) resource to reference the storage account via ID instead of name:

```diff
 resource "azurerm_storage_container" "this" {
   name               = "reproduce-storage-blob-account-reference-bug"
-  storage_account_name = azurerm_storage_account.this.name
+  storage_account_id = azurerm_storage_account.this.id
 }
```

This _also_ fails, because now we have inadvertently broken the `azurerm_storage_blob` resource's reference to the storage account, since the `storage_account_name` property is no longer exposed by the `azurerm_storage_container` resource (presumably since we no longer pass it as an argument).

```
Terraform planned the following actions, but then encountered a problem:
Error: Missing required argument

  with azurerm_storage_blob.this,
  on main.tf line 23, in resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this":
  23:   storage_account_name   = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_name

The argument "storage_account_name" is required, but no definition was found.

  # azurerm_storage_container.this will be updated in-place
  ~ resource "azurerm_storage_container" "this" {
        id                                = "https://reproducestorageblobbug.blob.core.windows.net/reproduce-storage-blob-account-reference-bug"
        name                              = "reproduce-storage-blob-account-reference-bug"
      + storage_account_id                = "/subscriptions/***/resourceGroups/reproduce-storage-blob-bug/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/reproducestorageblobbug"
      - storage_account_name              = "reproducestorageblobbug" -> null
        # (7 unchanged attributes hidden)
    }

Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.

Warning: Deprecated attribute

  on main.tf line 23, in resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this":
  23:   storage_account_name   = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_name

The attribute "storage_account_name" is deprecated. Refer to the provider
documentation for details.
```

### Expected Behaviour

I expected the `azurerm_storage_blob` resource type to accept the `storage_account_id` parameter once the `azurerm_storage_container` resource type did. _Particularly_ given the warning:

> ```
> Warning: Deprecated attribute
> 
>   on main.tf line 22, in resource "azurerm_storage_blob" "this":
>   22:   storage_account_name   = azurerm_storage_container.this.storage_account_name
> 
> The attribute "storage_account_name" is deprecated. Refer to the provider
> documentation for details.
> ```

Failing that, I expected the `azurerm_storage_container` to deduce the storage account name _from_ the `storage_account_id` argument, so that the `storage_account_name` property could still be exposed and not break existing references to it.

Having to go through and update _which resource_ the `azurerm_storage_blob` references in order to specify its storage account was unexpected, and should be unnecessary.

### Actual Behaviour

It is currently not possible to stop referencing an `azurerm_storage_container`'s storage account via the deprecated property `storage_account_name` (intending to replace it with a reference to `storage_account_id`) while there are still `azurerm_storage_blob` resources which reference the storage account _via_ the `azurerm_storage_container`. 

### Steps to Reproduce

Follow steps 1, 2 and 3 as outlined in the "Terraform Configuration Files" and "Debug Output" sections.

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 reaction to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* Please do not leave comments along the lines of "+1", "me too" or "any updates", they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritize the request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment and review the contribution guide to help.

### Description

When creating an `azurerm_api_management` resource with a V2 SKU (StandardV2, PremiumV2), setting `public_network_access_enabled = false` fails with:

```
ActivateServiceWithPrivateEndpointAccessNotAllowed: Blocking all public network access by setting
property `publicNetworkAccess` of API Management service ... is not enabled during service creation.
```

Azure requires V2 SKUs to be created with `publicNetworkAccess = true`, then updated to `false` after creation. The Azure Portal handles this transparently, but Terraform sends everything in a single PUT on creation.

### Current workaround

Users must resort to `azapi_update_resource` + `lifecycle { ignore_changes }`:

```hcl
resource "azurerm_api_management" "apim" {
  sku_name                      = "StandardV2_1"
  public_network_access_enabled = true  # forced, can't set false on creation

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [public_network_access_enabled]  # prevent plan ping-pong
  }
}

resource "azapi_update_resource" "disable_public_access" {
  type        = "Microsoft.ApiManagement/service@2024-05-01"
  resource_id = azurerm_api_management.apim.id

  body = {
    properties = {
      publicNetworkAccess = "Disabled"
    }
  }
}
```

This is fragile and adds unnecessary complexity.

### Proposed fix

The provider already does multi-step post-creation operations (sign_in, sign_up, tenant_access, soft-delete recovery). The same pattern can handle this.

In `api_management_resource.go`, after `CreateOrUpdateThenPoll` succeeds (~line 921), add:

```go
if strings.Contains(string(sku.Name), "V2") && publicNetworkAccess == apimanagementservice.PublicNetworkAccessDisabled {
    updatePayload := apimanagementservice.ApiManagementServiceUpdateParameters{
        Properties: &apimanagementservice.ApiManagementServiceUpdateProperties{
            PublicNetworkAccess: pointer.To(apimanagementservice.PublicNetworkAccessDisabled),
        },
    }
    if err := client.UpdateThenPoll(ctx, id, updatePayload); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("disabling public network access for V2 SKU %s: %+v", id, err)
    }
}
```

This forces `true` in the initial PUT for V2, then sends a PATCH to disable it — matching what the Azure Portal does.

### Description

We use terraform to create Windows Server images that have managed data disks.
In v0.11 with the Azure provider, when we subsequently make VMs from those images no mention of the managed disk snapshots is required....they simply come w/ the image.  In v0.12 we get the following error:

> Error: Error creating Windows Virtual Machine "BBVM1-vm" (Resource Group "BBVM1"): compute.VirtualMachinesClient#CreateOrUpdate: Failure sending request: StatusCode=400 -- Original Error: Code="InvalidParameter" Message="StorageProfile.dataDisks.lun does not have required value(s) for image specified in storage profile." Target="storageProfile"
>on modules\vm-base\main.tf line 47, in resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "config":
  47: resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "config" {

Our old v0.11 version

``` terraform
resource "azurerm_virtual_machine" "config" {
  count                            = "${contains(var.servers_needed, var.computer_name) ? 1 : 0}"
  name                             = "${local.name}-vm"
```

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl
resource "azurerm_api_management_product_api" "attach" {
  product_id = "test"
  api_name = "myAPI"
  api_management_name = "myAPImanager"
  resource_group_name = "rg"
}
```

### Expected Behavior

After creating an API and attaching it to a product with Terraform, one should be able to delete the API and, upon recreating it, the API should be attached to the product again.

### Actual Behavior

When recreating the API, Terraform creates the API succesfully, but does not see the need to add it to the product, so the API ends up with no product assignment. If one tries assigning it to a _different_ product however, this works successfully.

When performing the plan, terraform _does_ refresh the `product_api` state, but it thinks the API is still assigned to the product (from its previous assignment) so does not attempt to add it again.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Declare a new API with `azurerm_api_management_api`
1. Add the API to an existing product with `azurerm_api_management_product_api`
1. `terraform plan` & `apply`, the API is created and added successfully to the product
1. Manually remove the API from the API Management
1. Run `terraform plan --refresh=true` and `apply` again
1. Terraform recreates the API but does not assign it to a product
1. Repeat the above three steps but change the `product_id` to a different one, TF successfully adds it to the product

### Expected Behaviour

The `azurerm_api_management_api_operation_policy` as given should get accepted just like the `azurerm_api_management_api` based on the OpenAPI definition is accepted.

### Actual Behaviour

When running `terraform plan` the following error is logged and the operation fails:

```
╷
│ Error: "operation_id" may only contain alphanumeric characters and dashes up to 80 characters in length
│ 
│   with azurerm_api_management_api_operation_policy.openid-configuration,
│   on caching-policy.tf line 6, in resource "azurerm_api_management_api_operation_policy" "openid-configuration":
│    6:   operation_id        = "OpenIdRestResource_readOpenIdProviderMetadataOhneStage_get"
│ 
╵
```

I have read the documentation https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-api-import-restrictions#add-new-api-via-openapi-import and seen that the `operationId` value apparently gets normalized, even though this isn't explained in detail. The section https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-api-import-restrictions#export-api-as-openapi however explains what normalization rules get applied when exporting to OpenAPI.

I have tried to export an API which I previously imported from OpenAPI (via Terraform) and can confirm that `operationId` values containing `_` characters are left intact. From this I conclude that Azure API Management supports `_` (underscore) characters and that the validation applied by `azurerm_api_management_api_operation_policy` is too restrictive.

I expect to be able to repeatedly perform `terraform apply`.

### Actual Behaviour

When the VM Extension creation is successful but the run is not successful terraform returns the following error (for other extension types the error may differ):

> Error: Code="VMExtensionProvisioningError" Message="VM has reported a failure when processing extension 'dscconfigf31a30215b006a348a6f4276e732e0ee'. Error message: \"The DSC Extension received an incorrect input: A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'ScriptHash'.\r\n\r\nAnother common error is to specify parameters of type PSCredential without an explicit type. Please be sure to use a typed parameter in DSC Configuration, for example:\r\n\r\n    configuration Example {\r\n        param([PSCredential] $UserAccount)\r\n        ...\r\n    }.\r\nPlease correct the input and retry executing the extension.\"\r\n\r\nMore information on troubleshooting is available at https://aka.ms/VMExtensionDSCWindowsTroubleshoot "

The extension has been created in Azure at the point as exists with a provisioning state of `failed`.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1939288/104133226-1a762d00-537a-11eb-9fa6-31d7c7cdcce1.png)

However, Terraform has not tracked it's existence so when you next attempt a `terraform apply` the following error is presented:

> Error: A resource with the ID "/subscriptions/xxxxxxxxxxxx/resourceGroups/testenv21/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx-vm/extensions/dscconfigf31a30215b006a348a6f4276e732e0ee" already exists - to be managed via Terraform this resource needs to be imported into the State. Please see the resource documentation for "azurerm_virtual_machine_extension" for more information.

I think this error checking is to blame, it's treating deployment with an error on execution as a deployment error and assumes the extension wasn't created so no state is tracked.

https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/46da0a743a4dba74dd8514b580a6b79f0147d1d9/azurerm/internal/services/compute/virtual_machine_extension_resource.go#L165-L177

Is it possible to first track the creation by calling `d.SetId(*read.ID)` then return the provisioning error? If so I'm happy to update the code and submit a PR.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform apply` with the DSC extension (likely repos with other extensions) which containers a "runtime" error that will lead to the extension being created but `provisioning failed`
2. `terraform apply` and observe error

## Summary
The AzureRM Terraform provider produces an inconsistent final plan error when creating `azurerm_role_assignment` resources with blob container scopes. The provider changes the scope value format during apply, causing the operation to fail.

## Error Message
```
Error: Provider produced an inconsistent final plan

When expanding the plan for azurerm_role_assignment.databricks_read_access to
include new values learned so far during apply, provider
"registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm" produced an invalid new value for
.scope: was
cty.StringVal("https://xxx.blob.core.windows.net/connections"),
but now
cty.StringVal("/subscriptions/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxx/resourceGroups/xxx-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/xxx/blobServices/default/containers/connections").

This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's own
issue tracker.
```

## Expected Behavior
The provider should maintain consistent scope value formatting throughout the plan and apply phases. If the provider accepts a blob URL format for the scope, it should continue using that format consistently.

## Actual Behavior
The provider accepts the blob URL format (`https://xxx.blob.core.windows.net/connections`) during planning but then changes it to the full Azure resource path format (`/subscriptions/.../containers/connections`) during apply, causing an inconsistent final plan error.

## Environment Details
- **AzureRM Provider Version**: 4.41.0


## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create an `azurerm_role_assignment` resource with a scope pointing to a blob container using the blob URL format
2. Run `terraform plan` - this should succeed
3. Run `terraform apply` - this fails with the inconsistent final plan error

2nd attempt of apply is successful.

### Expected Behaviour

After rerun our terraform pipelines after Azure Key Vault access policies were altered in the Azure GUI, the service principal was either not able to read the secrets, or to add the access policies because it stated "The access policies are already existing". 

Now after refactoring the code to depend the certificate on the policies existing, manually delete all policies from the azure vault object, the certificate block tries to read the certificate despite the fact, that the access policy for the service principal of the pipeline run is still not existing and not created.

### Actual Behaviour

We expect that the depends_on block is respected, and every action on the resource "azurerm_key_vault_certificate" respects the depends_on, that the access policy is actually existing, is actually being reset to the terraform config, or is even recreated.

This should happen, respecting the depends_on block so before either data or resource block on azure key vault secrets/keys/certificates gets executed, the terraform code should ensure that the azure key vault access policies are according as defined in the terraform config.

### Steps to Reproduce

Use a service principal to apply terraform
Create a key vault, access policy for the service principal read and write certificates, a certificate block and store it in the key vault, a data block to read the certificate.
Delete the access policy through azure cli or gui
Reapply the terraform config and expect the access policy to get recreated BEFORE Terraform tries to access (read) the stored certificate.

Second approach:
Use a service principal to apply terraform
Create a key vault, access policy for the service principal to read and write certificates, a certificate block and store it in the key vault, a data block to read the certificate
Alter the access policy through azure cli or gui
Reapply the terraform config and expect the access policy to get reapplied as configured in the Terraform config to access the stored certificate.
Instead you get the error: "already exists - to be managed via Terraform this resource needs to be imported into the State. Please see the resource documentation for "azurerm_key_vault_access_policy" for more information."

> api_location: ""
> output_location: ""

Support for **app_location, api_location, and output_location** as configurable parameters required for various UI Framework such as **Reat, Vite** etc.

```
  repository_url      = var.repository_url
  repository_branch   = var.repository_branch
  repository_token    = var.github_token  
}
```

```
app_location
api_location
output_location
```

### Description

Azure supports two storage types for file shares, Standard and Premium, and Standard must be selected to enable geo-redundancy replication. azurerm_storage_account, however, supports only Premium storage for file shares thereby preventing the use of geo-redundancy replication. 

**The ask**: since Azure supports Standard storage for file shares, would it be possible for azurerm_storage_account to support it as well?

Details:
- azurerm_storage_account is used for creating a storage account
- account_kind arg is set to "FileStorage" to indicate the storage account will house file shares 
- account_tier arg must be set to "Premium" as stated in the [azurerm_storage_account](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/1.43.0/docs/resources/storage_account#account_tier-1) doc
- Any attempt to set account_tier to "Standard" results in error "_account_tier must be set to Premium for File Storage accounts_"
- Any attempt to set account_replication_type to "GRS" (geo-redundancy) results in error "_InvalidAccountType: AccountType Premium_GRS is invalid_"

### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Terraform used the selected providers to generate the following execution plan. Resource actions are indicated with the following symbols:
-/+ destroy and then create replacement

Terraform will perform the following actions:

  # azurerm_role_assignment.example must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_role_assignment" "example" {
      ~ id                               = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-example-avd-001/providers/Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/applicationgroups/vdag-example-desktop/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" -> (known after apply)
      ~ name                             = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" -> (known after apply)
        principal_id                     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
        role_definition_name             = "Desktop Virtualization User"
      ~ scope                            = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-example-avd-001/providers/Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/applicationgroups/vdag-example-desktop" -> "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-example-avd-001/providers/Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/applicationGroups/vdag-example-desktop" # forces replacement
      ~ skip_service_principal_aad_check = true -> (known after apply)
        # (2 unchanged attributes hidden)
    }

Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.
```

### Expected Behaviour

After importing an existing azurerm_role_assignment that references an Azure Virtual Desktop Application Group, running terraform plan should show no changes.

### Actual Behaviour

After importing the role assignment, Terraform detects a change in the scope attribute due to case sensitivity in the resource type path (applicationgroups vs applicationGroups), forcing an unnecessary replacement:

`~ scope = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-example-avd-001/providers/Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/applicationgroups/vdag-example-desktop" -> "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-example-avd-001/providers/Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/applicationGroups/vdag-example-desktop" # forces replacement`

### Steps to Reproduce

**1.** Create an azurerm_role_assignment manually in Azure Portal or via Azure CLI with a scope pointing to an AVD Application Group

**2.** Import the role assignment into Terraform state:

> terraform import azurerm_role_assignment.example "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-example-avd-001/providers/Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/applicationGroups/vdag-example-desktop/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"

**3.** Run terraform plan

**4.** Observe the forced replacement due to case difference in applicationgroups vs applicationGroups

### Important Factoids

This issue is similar to #23487 which was fixed in #23644 for resourcegroups vs resourceGroups. The same case-insensitive comparison logic should be applied to the Application Group resource type path.  When importing a role assignment, Azure returns the scope with lowercase applicationgroups, but the Terraform configuration typically uses the proper casing applicationGroups. Azure Resource Manager is case-insensitive for resource paths, so both refer to the same resource type.  The issue specifically occurs during the import process where the provider reads the scope from Azure with different casing than what's defined in the configuration.

Related PR fix: #23644

There is a disparity between what can be done regarding security rules management when you declare rules within a `azurerm_network_security_group` resource or if you do it by declaring `network_security_rule` resources rattached to a `azurerm_network_security_group`, e.g:

```

  name                = "xxxx-nsg"

    access                      = "Allow"
    protocol                    = "TCP"
    source_address_prefix       = "10.101.0.0/28"

    destination_address_prefix  = "*"
    destination_port_range      = "22"
  }
}
```

```
resource "azurerm_network_security_group" "xxxx-nsg" {
```

3.5.0

### Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_storage_account

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl
variable "zone" {
  default = "example.com"
}

variable "project" {
  default = "myproject"
}

variable "storagename" {
  default = "mystorageaccount"
}

resource "azurerm_dns_cname_record" "storage_account" {
  name                = join(".", ["data",var.project])
  zone_name           = var.zone
  resource_group_name = "dns_resource_group"
  record              = azurerm_storage_account.this.primary_web_host
  ttl                 = 3600
}

resource "azurerm_storage_account" "this" {
  name                     = var.storagename
  resource_group_name      = azurerm_resource_group.this.name
  location                 = azurerm_resource_group.this.location
  account_kind             = "StorageV2"
  account_tier             = "Standard"
  account_replication_type = "LRS"
  static_website {
    index_document     = "index.html"
    error_404_document = "error.html"
  }
  custom_domain {
    name = join(".", [azurerm_dns_cname_record.storage_account.name,azurerm_dns_cname_record.storage_account.zone_name])
  }
}
```


### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Error: Error creating Azure Storage Account "mystorageaccount": storage.AccountsClient#Create: Failure sending request: StatusCode=0 -- Original Error: autorest/azure: Service returned an error. Status=<nil> Code="StorageDomainNameCouldNotVerify" Message="The custom domain name could not be verified. CNAME mapping from data.myproject.example.com to any of mystorageaccount.blob.core.windows.net,mystorageaccount.z6.web.core.windows.net does not exist."
```


### Expected Behaviour

Apply should work in one step.

### Actual Behaviour

Error.

Alternatively, adding a `depends_on` block causes a cycle error, as you'd expect.

The issue here is that we obviously cannot reference the `primary_web_host` property before it's applied since that is only known after apply. While with some other endpoint types (e.g., blob) you can "calculate" the endpoint (e.g., you could do `join(".", [var.storagename, "blob.core.windows.net"])` in the `record` property of `azurerm_dns_cname_record`) provided there is no calculation based off of the other resource, you cannot do this with static websites because (as far as I can find, anyway) there is always a subdomain added to the fqdn of `z#`, e.g., `z6` in the example above (`mystorageaccount.z6.web.core.windows.net`) and that cannot be known beforehand.

This causes the apply to fail.

What is needed is a three-step process (behind the scenes) where the storage account is created, DNS record created, then `custom_domain` applied.

Obviously this might be difficult, because there's however many ways DNS records can get created out there, but a suggestion might be to build an implicit dependency on the `custom_domain` portion of the storage account apply on anything that references any of the `*_host` properties of the storage account in the rest of the config, which causes a split configuration to occur and the final `custom_domain` section of the apply cannot occur until those resources are created properly. If there aren't any of those references, then fire the entire config in one shot.

This could extend to any of the host properties, even if it's calculable, because being able to do this would be a much better approach than the "hacky" version of calculating things as mentioned above.

Alternatively, a new resource, e.g. `azurerm_storage_account_custom_domain` (similar to `azurerm_cdn_endpoint_custom_domain`) could be used with this, which would permit a more obvious dependency chain.

### Steps to Reproduce

- terraform plan
- terraform apply

### Description

Right now, creating a new `azurerm_key_vault_certificate` does not support creating an EV-SSL certificate.

According to the [API docs](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/keyvault/certificates/get-certificate-policy/get-certificate-policy#issuerparameters), that capability is exposed via the `issuer_parameters` block of the policy. As of [right](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/e78afc8da364f676a7873d16ae39a1ff323bf76f/internal/services/keyvault/key_vault_certificate_resource.go#L104) [now](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/key_vault_certificate#issuer_parameters), the `azurerm_key_vault_certificate` `certificate_parameters` `issuer_parameters` block only supports `name` and not `certificate_type` (which is what I expect the underlying API `cty` parameter to map to since that's what it's called everywhere else, e.g., in the Portal, via PowerShell, etc.) or `cert_transparency`.

This ability would be beneficial. 

Obviously this should not be relevant for non-integrated CA issuers that can't do this, so it should probably be limited to non "Self" or "Unknown" `name`s.

```hcl
# where security rules are managed via separate azurerm_network_security_rule resources.

  name                = "nsg-example"
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name

  tags = var.tags

  priority                    = 100

  access                      = "Allow"

  source_port_range           = "*"
  destination_port_range      = "443"
  source_address_prefix       = "*"
  destination_address_prefix  = "*"
  resource_group_name         = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  network_security_group_name = azurerm_network_security_group.example.name
}

variable "tags" {
  type = map(string)
  default = {
    Environment = "Production"
    # Changing any tag value (e.g. casing) triggers the bug
    Shutdown-Disabled = "yes"  # was "Yes" previously
  }
}
```

### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Error: creating/updating Network Security Group (Subscription: "xxxxx-xxxxx"
│ Resource Group Name: "rg-example"
│ Network Security Group Name: "nsg-example"): performing CreateOrUpdate: unexpected status 400 (200) with error:
│ InvalidRequestFormat: Cannot parse the request.
│
│   with azurerm_network_security_group.example,
│   on main.tf line 1, in resource "azurerm_network_security_group" "example":
│    1: resource "azurerm_network_security_group" "example" {


The Terraform plan shows **only tag changes** on the NSG (no security rule changes):


  ~ resource "azurerm_network_security_group" "example" {
        id                  = "/subscriptions/.../nsg-example"
        name                = "nsg-example"
      ~ tags                = {
          ~ "Shutdown-Disabled" = "Yes" -> "yes"
        }
    }
```

### Expected Behaviour

Updating only the `tags` on an `azurerm_network_security_group` should succeed with a 200 response. The PUT request body should correctly serialize any existing security rules (including those managed by separate `azurerm_network_security_rule` resources or externally by services like Azure Databricks).

### Actual Behaviour

The Azure REST API returns `400 InvalidRequestFormat: Cannot parse the request`, indicating the PUT request body is malformed. This happens even though the only planned change is tag casing normalization — no security rule modifications are planned.

The issue affects **all** NSGs being updated in the same apply, regardless of whether they have externally-managed rules (e.g., Databricks-injected rules) or only Terraform-managed rules.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an `azurerm_network_security_group` with **no inline `security_rule` blocks**
2. Create one or more `azurerm_network_security_rule` resources associated with the NSG
3. Apply successfully (initial creation works)
4. Change **only a tag value** on the NSG (e.g., change casing from `"Yes"` to `"yes"`)
5. Run `terraform apply`
6. Observe the 400 error

The issue is more reliably reproduced when the NSG also has security rules injected by external services (e.g., Azure Databricks workspace rules), but may also occur with only Terraform-managed rules.

### Important Factoids

This issue was introduced in **v4.71.0**, which includes PR #30913 that changed the `security_rule` TypeSet hash function (`hashNetworkSecurityRule`) and added `DiffSuppressFunc` for case-insensitive ASG ID comparison. The same NSGs were successfully managed with **v4.70.0** and earlier versions.

### References

- #30913 — PR that introduced the `hashNetworkSecurityRule` hash function change in v4.71.0
- #29841 — Original issue for ASG case sensitivity that #30913 addresses
- The bug is **not fixed** in v4.72.0, v4.73.0, v4.74.0, or v4.75.0 — none of these releases contain NSG-related changes

### Expected Behaviour

The default value for this property should be `null`, and the user should be able to set `null` as a value.

### Actual Behaviour

Value can only be `true` or `false`.

This setting is not configurable via the azure portal nor the azure cli. It is only configurable via an ARM/Bicep template.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.web/staticsites?pivots=deployment-language-bicep#staticsite

According to the template, an empty string is a legal value, and should set the resource configuration property to `null`.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5609685-acde-463f-a4b3-8f92729e2507)

The default value when creating a static web app via the azure portal is `null`.

This affects the behavior of the static web app when adding a private endpoint. The expected behavior, and the behavior that I believe the `null` value achieves, is that public network access is allowed in the absence of a private endpoint, and it is blocked when a private endpoint is configured. This lines up with the azure documentation about securing a static web app on a private subnet.

However when the property is explicitly set to "Enabled" (`true` value in terraform) it overrides this behavior and you cannot disable public network access except by applying the explicit `false` value via terraform.

### Expected Behaviour

History of these resources:

* we converted to using azurerm_windows_virtual_machine and separate azurerm_managed_disk
* we expected the Resource Group Names to be the same for each - but due to MS defect we get a capitalised name for the disk RG.

After refactoring code to use the new VM resources type, and re-importing the resources into Terraform State, we expected zero change.
However the plan output suggests recreation of disk is required to fix the RG name issue.

Current Work Around:
* use this in the azurerm_managed_disk resource
  * resource_group_name     = upper(azurerm_resource_group.main.name)

Azure has this open issue: https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/issues/36222
It is very inconvenient, but seems to be stalled.
I'm hoping we can work around this issue in Terrafrom by treating the field as case insensitive when creating execution plan.
It would be helpful if resource 'azurerm_managed_disk' treated argument 'resource_group_name' as case insensitive during planning phase.

Currently when I run 'terraform plan' on a disk, the plan suggests that resource must be replaced due to a change in this field.

I currently have to specify this in my code:
resource_group_name     = upper(azurerm_resource_group.main.name)

```
  # azurerm_managed_disk.datadisk must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_managed_disk" "datadisk" {
      ~ resource_group_name           = "RG-UKS-IT-DE2-XXX" -> "rg-uks-it-de2-xxx" # forces replacement

    }
```

```shell
planned set element cty.ObjectVal(map[string]cty.Value{"access":cty.StringVal("Allow"), "description":cty.StringVal(""), "destination_address_prefix":cty.StringVal("VirtualNetwork"),
"destination_address_prefixes":cty.SetValEmpty(cty.String), "destination_application_security_group_ids":cty.SetValEmpty(cty.String), "destination_port_range":cty.StringVal(""),
"destination_port_ranges":cty.SetVal([]cty.Value{cty.StringVal("443"), cty.StringVal("80")}), "direction":cty.StringVal("Inbound"), "name":cty.StringVal("ClusterOutboundPublic"), "priority":cty.NumberIntVal(102),

"source_port_range":cty.StringVal("*"), "source_port_ranges":cty.SetValEmpty(cty.String)}) does not correlate with any element in actual.
```

### Expected Behaviour

When a `security_rule` in `azurerm_network_security_group` uses a computed value for `source_address_prefix` (e.g., from `data.azurerm_public_ip.main.ip_address`), and a dependency resource is updated (causing the computed value to be unknown during planning), Terraform should:

1. Successfully plan the change
2. Apply the change
3. During plan expansion, correctly correlate the planned Set element (with unknown `source_address_prefix`) with the actual Set element (with known `source_address_prefix`)
4. Complete successfully without errors

### Actual Behaviour

Terraform fails during plan expansion with the following error:

```
Error: Provider produced inconsistent final plan
```
The error occurs because:
- During planning: `source_address_prefix` is `cty.UnknownVal(cty.String)` (computed from data source)
- After apply: `source_address_prefix` becomes a known value (e.g., `"20.23.90.115/32"`)
- Terraform Core's Set correlation fails because a known value is never equivalent to an unknown value (per `values_equiv.go` in Terraform SDK)

### Steps to Reproduce


1. Initialize and apply with initial IP range:
```bash
terraform init
terraform apply -var='authorized_ip_ranges=["1.2.3.4/32"]'
```

2. Change the authorized IP range to trigger the error:
```bash
terraform apply -var='authorized_ip_ranges=["5.6.7.8/32"]'
```

3. Observe the "Provider produced inconsistent final plan" error during apply.

_No response_

This issue specifically addresses computed values in `source_address_prefix` (string) causing Set correlation failures.

### Expected Behaviour

The `azurerm_key_vault_secret` resources are stored in the TF state correctly and the TF script succeeds.

### Actual Behaviour

The `azurerm_key_vault_secret` resources are created in the Key Vault, but *not* stored in the TF state due to TF thinking that the root resource (i.e. the Key Vault) has been deleted. The TF script fails.

### Steps to Reproduce

- Have at least 2 TF scripts with each having its own state.
- Have the first script create the Key Vault.
- Have the second script create a secret in the Key Vault just using a string for the ID of the Key Vault created in the first script.
- Ensure the first script creates the Key Vault in region A e.g. eastus.
- Ensure the second script runs on a machine with an IP that is **not** in region A, somewhere like uksouth.

### Important Factoids

- There are separate Terraform scripts each with their own state.
- One script creates the Key Vault.
- The other script(s) create secrets using a string for the Key Vault ID.
- The Terraform scripts are run on GitHub Actions.
- GitHub Actions runners run in the US on Azure infrastructure (https://github.community/t/github-runners-physical-location/162436)
- When the runner is based in eastus, the same location that the Key Vault is being created, the scripts work.
- When the runner is **not** based in eastus, the scripts fail with this error.
- I think it might be something to do with this issue here - https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/406413/azure-rest-api-response-results-depend-on-requeste.html

### Affected Resource(s)

<!--- Please list the affected resources and data sources. --->

* azurerm_storage_account

### Expected Behavior

While creating or applying an execution plan no sensitive data should be printed into the console logs. This is very important in case TF is running as part of a CI/CD pipeline.

### Actual Behavior

If TF detects a change on a `azurerm_storage_account` resource and needs to recreate it then sensitive data such as the `primary access key` for the current active storage accounts gets printed in clear text into the console. This is very critical if your CI/CD pipeline just performed the planning step but did not execute yet the plan as in our case sometimes a manual approval is required before we allow the execution of the plan. As the current active `primary access key` gets revealed anybody with access to the console logs is now able to infiltrate the storage account.

List of attributes that should be marked as sensitive to avoid this issue:

- primary_access_key
- primary_blob_connection_string
- primary_connection_string
- secondary_access_key
- secondary_blob_connection_string
- secondary_connection_string

<!--- Please list the steps required to reproduce the issue. --->

1. `terraform apply`
2. Change some attribute that causes an recreation of the storage account resource (e.g. changing the name)
3. `terraform plan`

* `azurerm_application_gateway.probe.match`-blocks

### Terraform Configuration Files

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

An application gateway configuration that uses this `probe` and `match` blocks:
```hcl
  probe {
    name                = "http_probe${var.prod_domain_suffix}"
    host                = "probe${var.prod_domain_suffix}"
    path                = "/"
    protocol            = "Http"
    interval            = 60
    timeout             = 15
    unhealthy_threshold = 2
    minimum_servers     = 2
    match {
      status_code = ["100-999"]
      body        = ""
    }
  }
```

### Expected Behavior

The "http response body match" field on Azure should be empty when the body property is set to empty.

### Actual Behavior

The "http response body match" field on Azure is set to `*` when the body property is explicitly set to empty. Unfortunately, Azure only looks for the presence of the field value in the response and does not evaluate expressions. So, `*` means that an asterisk must be in the response body and does _not_ mean 'everything'.

I also suggest to change the default value of `body` from `*` to empty.

### Description

Following documentation, we are changing the usage of azurerm_virtual_machine for azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.
We need to use the winrm listener.
According to [azurerm_virtual_machine resource documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/virtual_machine#protocol), protocol of winrm listener can be HTTP or HTTPS in uppercase.
According to [azurerm_windows_virtual_machine resource documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/windows_virtual_machine#Protocol), protocol of winrm listener can be Http or Https in camelcase.

In order to have our infrastructure matching up-to-date code, we want to migrate from azurerm_virtual_machine to azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.

Code is updated accordingly:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_virtual_machine" "vm" {
# other mandatory config is done
  os_profile_windows_config {
    winrm {
      protocol = "HTTP"
    }
  }
}
```
Becomes:
```hcl
resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "vm" {
# other mandatory config is done
  winrm_listener {
    protocol = "Http"
  }
}
```

then we run terraform commands:
```bash
terraform state show azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm
# azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm:
resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "vm" {
...
    id                         = "/subscriptions/XXXX/resourceGroups/XXXX/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/MigrateWinVM"
...
}
terraform state rm azurerm_virtual_machine.vm
...
terraform import azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm "/subscriptions/XXXX/resourceGroups/XXXX/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/MigrateWinVM"
...
Import successful!
...
```

But next tf plan runs tells:
```bash
  # azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "vm" {
...
      - winrm_listener { # forces replacement
          - protocol = "HTTP" -> null
        }
      + winrm_listener { # forces replacement
          + protocol = "Http"
        }
}
```

Next configuration is not valid (tf plan outputs an error):
```hcl
resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "vm" {
# other mandatory config is done
  winrm_listener {
    protocol = "HTTP"
  }
}
```


### Description / Feedback

case change should not be detected as # forces replacement.
OR
azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.winrm_listener.protocol should accept UPPERCASE configuration.

But you may have a better procedure to migrate from azurerm_virtual_machine to azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.
Can terraform 1.1.0 handle this ?

A quick action though is to update [azurerm_virtual_machine resource documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/virtual_machine#protocol) : `(Required) Specifies the protocol of listener. Possible values are Http or Https.` which is a valid configuration.
That documentation fix will allow people to not have the same issue than me.

<!--- Thank you for keeping this note for the community --->


### Description

tl;dr:
I am looking for a way to control the `private_dns_zone_group` configuration of an `azurerm_private_endpoint` with Azure policy.
The way the provider is currently implemented, the externally created config is overwritten every time and cannot be preserved.  
Therefore, I propose the flag `preserve_existing_dns_config` to exclude this configuration from Terraform.

Long read:
The Azure Cloud Adoption Framework/Enterprise Scale outlines multiple options for private DNS management of private endpoints.
One of them looks like this:

- One central connectivity subscription hosts all private-link hosted zones. This way, the DNS zones can be resolved by multiple spokes.
- Workload subscriptions and their users are able to create private Endpoints within their spoke but do not have permissions to "join" the central private DNS zones.
- Therefore, an Azure policy is deployed to manage the central DNS. It scans for private endpoints and creates the missing DNS config as well as joining them to the central DNS zone.
See: [azure-docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/azure-best-practices/private-link-and-dns-integration-at-scale#private-link-and-dns-integration-in-hub-and-spoke-network-architectures)


The current implementation of `azurerm_private_endpoint` poses a challenge. If the `private_dns_zone_group` block isn't included, it results in the deletion of the existing private_dns_zone_group configuration. Conversely, defining the `private_dns_zone_group` triggers an attempt to enforce a configuration that is beyond the spoke's permission. Consequently, this setup prevents the use of an externally configured DNS management policy when the resource is under Terraform's management.

Proposal:
Add a flag to ignore existing `private_dns_zone_group`.


Workarounds:
I tired a few things to get around this, but none of them are idempotent.  

0. Lifecycle rule - cant be conditional. Not an option

1. Quick and Easy:
- Apply `azurerm_private_endpoint` configuration using terraform
- Apply policy to generate DNS config
- Hardcode DNS config into existing `azurerm_private_endpoint` configuration

2. Quick and less easy:
- Metode No.1, but in terraform with azapi resoruces.
- Apply `azurerm_private_endpoint` configuration using terraform
- Apply policy to generate DNS config
- Enable the `preserve_existing_dns_config` attribute.
- Use azapi to figure out the current config and patch the `azurerm_private_endpoint` on the fly.

This can not be idempotent though, because the terraform dependency tree can not check for a resource with azcli in plan phase.
(there are multiple ways to check, tried a lot of them. Every one had some problem with the dependency tree. Attached my last attempt.)
Original module code can be found [here](https://github.com/aztfmod/terraform-azurerm-caf/tree/main/modules/networking/private_endpoint)

My code:
```
resource "azurecaf_name" "pep" {
  name          = var.name
  resource_type = "azurerm_private_endpoint"
  prefixes      = var.global_settings.prefixes
  random_length = var.global_settings.random_length
  clean_input   = true
  passthrough   = var.global_settings.passthrough
  use_slug      = var.global_settings.use_slug
}

resource "azurerm_private_endpoint" "pep" {
  name                = azurecaf_name.pep.result
  location            = local.location
  resource_group_name = local.resource_group_name
  subnet_id           = var.subnet_id
  tags                = local.tags

  private_service_connection {
    name                           = var.settings.private_service_connection.name
    private_connection_resource_id = var.resource_id
    is_manual_connection           = try(var.settings.private_service_connection.is_manual_connection, false)
    subresource_names              = var.settings.private_service_connection.subresource_names
    request_message                = try(var.settings.private_service_connection.request_message, null)
  }

  dynamic "private_dns_zone_group" {
    for_each = can(var.settings.private_dns) ? [var.settings.private_dns] : []

    content {
      name = lookup(private_dns_zone_group.value, "zone_group_name", "default")
      private_dns_zone_ids = concat(
        flatten([
          for key in try(private_dns_zone_group.value.keys, []) : [
            try(var.private_dns[try(private_dns_zone_group.value.lz_key, var.client_config.landingzone_key)][key].id, [])
          ]
          ]
        ),
        lookup(private_dns_zone_group.value, "ids", [])
      )
    }
  }
  dynamic "private_dns_zone_group" {
    for_each = can(var.settings.preserve_existing_dns_config) && local.pe_exists ? try(local.private_dns_zones_ids) : {}

    content {
      name = "default"
      private_dns_zone_ids = try(private_dns_zone_group.value, [])
    }
  }



  dynamic "ip_configuration" {
    for_each = try(var.settings.ip_configurations, {})

    content {
      name               = ip_configuration.value.name
      private_ip_address = ip_configuration.value.private_ip_address
      subresource_name   = lookup(ip_configuration.value, "subresource_name", null)
      member_name        = lookup(ip_configuration.value, "member_name", null)
    }
  }
}

# get the azurerm_resource_group id from name
data "azurerm_resource_group" "pep_rg" {
  name = local.resource_group_name
}

# get a list of all private endpoints to check if they are already created (kind of redundant, as this cant be read in plan)
data "azapi_resource_list" "private_endpoints" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints@2023-06-01"
  parent_id = format("%s",data.azurerm_resource_group.pep_rg.id)
  response_export_values = ["*"]
}

# get the privateDnsZoneGroups of the current PE
data "azapi_resource_list" "dns_zone_groups" {
  for_each = try(local.pe_exists, false) ? {yes = true} : {}
  type      = "Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/privateDnsZoneGroups@2023-06-01"
  parent_id = format("%s/providers/Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/%s",data.azurerm_resource_group.pep_rg.id, azurecaf_name.pep.result)
  response_export_values = ["*"]
}

# extract config from azapi data
locals {
  private_dns_zones_ids = try({ for config, data in jsondecode(data.azapi_resource_list.dns_zone_groups["yes"].output).value[0].properties.privateDnsZoneConfigs :
    data.name => [data.properties.privateDnsZoneId]
  }, {})
  available_pe = [for pe in jsondecode(data.azapi_resource_list.private_endpoints.output).value:
    pe.name
  ]
  pe_exists = try(var.settings.preserve_existing_dns_config, false) ? contains(local.available_pe, azurecaf_name.pep.result) : false
}

# some debug output. Use with caution, can break dependencies
resource "null_resource" "debug_output" {
  # Changes to any instance of the cluster requires re-provisioning
  triggers = {
    #raw_api_response = data.azapi_resource_list.dns_zone_groups.output
    raw_api_response_pe = data.azapi_resource_list.private_endpoints.output
    available_pe = try(jsonencode(local.available_pe), [])
    #privateDnsZoneId = jsondecode(data.azapi_resource_list.dns_zone_groups.output).value[0].properties.privateDnsZoneConfigs[0].properties.privateDnsZoneId
    #local = jsonencode(local.private_dns_zones_ids)
    #[0].properties.privateDnsZoneId
  }
}
```

### Community Note

When running azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association Terraform resource on a subnet with already attached NSG, the wrong error appears:
`Error: A resource with the ID "/subscriptions/<subscription_id>/resourceGroups/<resource_group>/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/<vnet>/subnets/<subnet>" already exists - to be managed via Terraform this resource needs to be imported into the State. Please see the resource documentation for "azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association" for more information.`

The error indicates that there's an issue with the subnet not being managed by Terraform but that's wrong, it is managed by Terraform.
The correct error should be something like: "Subnet have already Network Security Group attached".
Manually removing the NSG association on the subnet and running Terraform again solved it.

### Affected Resource(s)

### Terraform Configuration Files

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

```hcl
resource "azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting" "kv_monitor" {
  name                       = "kv-monitor-diagnostics"
  target_resource_id         = azurerm_key_vault.key_vault.id
  log_analytics_workspace_id = var.log_analytics_workspace_id

  log {
    category = "AuditEvent"
    enabled  = true
  }

  metric {
    category = "AllMetrics"
  }
}
```

### Expected Behaviour

After successfully applying these changes, re-running `terraform plan` should not show any changes.

### Actual Behaviour

Re-running `terraform plan` results in a diff as terraform believes it needs to remove the default `retention_policy` that is stored off in the state.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting that sends diagnostics to a key vault.
2. `terraform apply`
3. Run `terraform apply` again.

### Important Factoids

The documentation Azure Monitor diagnostics settings says that the retention policy only applies when sending the data to a Storage Account: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/diagnostic-settings

The Terraform documentation for the provider says the `retention_policy` is optional: https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/monitor_diagnostic_setting

### Description

In Azure you can create a Private Link Service on an Application Gateway and after that, create a Private Endpoint to the PLS using the following construct:

```hcl
resource "azurerm_private_endpoint" "pe" {
  name                = "${local.name_prefix}-gw-pe"
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.rg.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.rg.name
  subnet_id           = data.azurerm_subnet.mgmt.id

  private_service_connection {
    name                           = "${local.name_prefix}-xxx-pe"
    private_connection_resource_id = "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/rg/providers/Microsoft.Network/applicationGateways/waf-apigw"
    is_manual_connection = false
    subresource_names = [
      "apigw-feip01"
    ]
  }
}
```

Azure CLI has the ability to add a Private Link Resource to the Application Gateway:

### Affected resource

`azurerm_subnet` — `delegation.service_delegation.actions`

### Description

The Azure REST API specification marks `ServiceDelegationPropertiesFormat.actions` as `readOnly: true`. However, the AzureRM provider exposes it as an optional configurable attribute rather than a computed attribute.

This allows Terraform to plan changes to a property that the API defines as server-managed.

### API specification

In API version `2025-09-01`, the `actions` property is defined as:

    "actions": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "The actions permitted to the service upon delegation.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "readOnly": true
    }

[Microsoft Network API specification — actions is read-only](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/main/specification/network/resource-manager/Microsoft.Network/Network/stable/2025-09-01/virtualNetwork.json#L20517-L20524)

This concerns only `actions`; the delegation's `serviceName` remains configurable.

### Provider implementation

The same relevant implementation is present in the latest release inspected, AzureRM 5.6.0:

- `actions` is declared as `Optional`, without `Computed`.
- `expandSubnetDelegation()` copies configured actions into the API request model.
- `flattenSubnetDelegation()` reads the API-returned actions into state.

[Provider source — subnet_resource.go](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v5.6.0/internal/services/network/subnet_resource.go)

The provider documentation also acknowledges:

> Azure may add default actions depending on the service delegation name and they can't be changed.

[Provider documentation](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v5.6.0/website/docs/r/subnet.html.markdown)

### Observed behavior

With AzureRM 4.x, we updated an existing subnet delegated to `Microsoft.Network/applicationGateways`, changing its configured action from:

    Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action

to:

    Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/action

Terraform planned an in-place update and apply completed successfully. However, a subsequent direct ARM GET still returned only `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action`.

The configured action list was therefore not reflected in the API readback.

The latest release was inspected at source level, not runtime-tested.

### Expected behavior

Model `actions` as a computed-only attribute populated from the Azure API response, with an appropriate migration path for existing configurations.

Terraform should report the actions assigned by Azure rather than plan updates to a read-only property.

### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Error: 1 error occurred:
        * cannot configure 'queue_properties' when the Provider Feature 'data_plane_available' is set to 'false'
```

### Expected Behaviour

Switching `data_plane_available` to `false` and changing nothing should work if none of `queue_properties` and `static_websites` are set in the `storage_account` else it should fail as now.

Thus changing the provider confifuguration only on the example above should give

```
No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.
```


### Actual Behaviour

```
Error: 1 error occurred:
        * cannot configure 'queue_properties' when the Provider Feature 'data_plane_available' is set to 'false'
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Apply with `data_plane_available` set to `true` or unspecified
Apply again with `data_plane_available` set to `false`

### Important Factoids

`queue_properties` and `static_websites` are computed attributes, thus even when not set in input if data plane is enabled (which is the default behavior thus valid for existing resources) then the result gets stored into the statefile.

The read method for this resource should nullify the 2 attributes if data plane is disabled instead of doing nothing. This would solve this case and still return the error if any of `queue_properties` or `static_websites` is set in the resource.

Note #1: I will submit a PR implementing above-mentioned change

Note #2: a corner case to this implementation is that if at the same time one of this attribute is removed and the provider switches from true to false then the related config on Azure side might be kept as is and never touched by TF again. But this is a balance between "I need to disable data plane calls because of new security constraints and I don't use those features and I don't want to destroy my resources for this" and a corner case that is not likely to happen.
