### Description

The default behaviour of the Azure Platform (and Terraform today) when the deleting a Resource Group is to delete all of the items within this Resource Group.

Whilst this feature makes it easy to clean-up any resources - since resources can be provisioned outside of Terraform, it means that these Resources are untracked by Terraform - and so Terraform is unable to show these Resources in the Plan during the deletion of the Resource Group.

Terraform currently has a feature-flag for this behaviour available within the Features block today - which will check during the deletion of the Resource Group for any Resources within this Resource Group, and raise an error (stating these must be removed first) if any Resources are found. In v2.x versions of the Azure Provider this is disabled by default - however for v3.0 we intend to flip this default to be enabled by default.

* azurerm_resource_group

### Potential Terraform Configuration

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

To retain the existing behaviour the following can be used
```hcl
provider "azurerm" {
  features {
    resource_group {
      prevent_deletion_if_contains_resources = false
    }
  }
}
```

### Description

In cases where a module should support using a predefined IP Address (such as one from a whitelist) but default to creating its own, it would be beneficial to have the azurerm_public_ip return the name of the public ip address created. In the below example where count is used, the name ends up being lost and exposing that through an output ends up being rather difficult since it needs to be created elsewhere via interpolation. 

In my use case I'm exposing the names of the public IPs so that I can look up individual IPs to get their addresses for DNS.

The alternative is that the data source azurerm_public_ips exposes the ip address for each resource but I suspect that this is just returning the results from the API.

data "azurerm_public_ips" "this" {

  name_prefix         = "${var.public_ip_prefix_name}"

  count = "${var.public_ip_prefix_name != "" ? length(data.azurerm_public_ips.this.public_ips) : var.count}"
  name                = "${var.hostname}-nic-${count.index}"
  location            = "${var.location}"

    public_ip_address_id          = "${var.public_ip_prefix_name != "" ? element(data.azurerm_public_ips.this.public_ips.*.id, count.index) : element(concat(azurerm_public_ip.public_ip.*.id, list("")), count.index)}"

resource "azurerm_public_ip" "public_ip" {

  location                     = "${var.location}"

With the current version of the AzureRM provider it is not possible to create an API in Azure API Management with the type "odata".
With the azapi_resource below it is possible to create an OData API in Azure API Management, but it seems that the azurerm provider does not support this.

```terraform
resource "azapi_resource" "test_odata_api" {
  type      = "Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/apis@2023-05-01-preview"
  name      = "test_odata_api;rev=1"
  parent_id = data.azurerm_api_management.api_management.id
  body = jsonencode({
    properties = {
      apiRevision            = "1"
      apiRevisionDescription = "Revision 1 of Test Odata API"
      apiType                = "odata"
      apiVersion             = "v1"
      apiVersionDescription  = "Version 1 of Test Odata API"
      displayName            = "Test Odata API"
      format                 = "odata"
      path                   = "my/odata/api"
      serviceUrl             = "https://my-odata-service.com"
      protocols = [
        "https"
      ]
      type  = "odata"
      value = file("odata_api_definition.xml")
    }
  })
}
```

Currently supported `api_type` values: `graphql`, `http`, `soap`, `websocket`
Currently supported `content_format` values for `import`-blocks: `openapi`, `openapi+json`, `openapi+json-link`, `openapi-link`, `swagger-json`, `swagger-link-json`, `wadl-link-json`, `wadl-xml`, `wsdl` and `wsdl-link`

I would expect there to be an additional `api_type` `odata` as well as an additional `content_format` value `odata` or `odata-link` as documented in the Azure documentation (see link in references).

  name                  = "example"
  resource_group_name   = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location              = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  size                  = "Standard_DS1_v2"
  network_interface_ids = [azurerm_network_interface.example.id]

  # Specialized image from Azure Compute Gallery - no admin credentials needed
  source_image_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/galleries/myGallery/images/myImage/versions/1.0.0"

  os_disk {
    caching              = "ReadWrite"
    storage_account_type = "Standard_LRS"
  }
}
```

### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Error: creating Windows Virtual Machine (Subscription: "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
Resource Group Name: "example"
Virtual Machine Name: "example"): performing CreateOrUpdate:
unexpected status 400 (400 Bad Request) with error: InvalidParameter:
Parameter OSProfile is not allowed with a specialized image.

  on main.tf line 13:
  13: resource "azurerm_windows_virtual_machine" "example"
```

### Expected Behaviour

When source_image_id references a specialized image (os_state = Specialized in the
Azure Compute Gallery), the provider should omit OSProfile entirely from the
CreateOrUpdate API request, as Azure requires. The VM should be created successfully
without admin_username, admin_password, or computer_name being specified.

### Actual Behaviour

The provider always sends OSProfile (containing admin_username, admin_password,
computer_name, and WindowsConfiguration) in the API request regardless of image type.
Azure returns 400 Bad Request: InvalidParameter - "Parameter OSProfile is not allowed
with a specialized image."

Additionally, the admin_username field uses ExactlyOneOf: ["admin_username",
"os_managed_disk_id"] in the schema, making it effectively required when source_image_id
is used — preventing users from omitting credentials even when they should.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a specialized Windows image version in an Azure Compute Gallery
   (azurerm_shared_image with specialized = true)
2. Attempt to deploy azurerm_windows_virtual_machine using source_image_id
   pointing to that specialized image version
3. Run terraform apply
4. Observe 400 Bad Request: OSProfile is not allowed with a specialized image

### Important Factoids

This affects any deployment using specialized images from Azure Compute Gallery. Specialized images are commonly used when cloning pre-configured VMs (e.g. domain-joined, pre-installed software) where re-running sysprep/generalization is not desired. The Azure REST API has always explicitly rejected OSProfile for specialized images — this is documented Azure behaviour, not a new API change.

### References

- PR with fix: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/pull/32345
- Azure API docs on specialized images: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/shared-image-galleries?tabs=azure-cli#generalized-and-specialized-images
- Azure REST API spec (OSProfile not allowed with specialized): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/compute/virtual-machines/create-or-update

### Description

Add support for specifying a `azurerm_storage_encryption_scope` when creating a `azurerm_storage_container`.  It looks like the base resources for defining an encryption scope were added in #8893.  One mode of using an encryption scope is to choose a scope when [defining a blob storage container](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/encryption-scope-manage?tabs=portal).  To do this, the `azurerm_storage_container` resource needs to support adding an encryption scope.  

It appears (from my cursory reading of code) that there's already support for this in the underlying Azure Go SDK in the [ContainerProperties](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go@v55.0.0+incompatible/services/storage/mgmt/2021-02-01/storage#ContainerProperties) object.

```hcl
resource "azurerm_api_management" "api-management" {
  location            = "East US"
  name                = "contoso-apimgmt"
  publisher_email     = "publisher@contoso.com"
  publisher_name      = "Contoso"
  resource_group_name = "rg"

  identity {
    type = "SystemAssigned"
  }

  sku_name = "Developer_1"

  tags = local.common_tags

  policy {
    xml_content = <<XML
  <policies>
    <inbound>
        <cors>
            <allowed-origins>
              %{for origin in var.cors_origins~}
                <origin>${origin}</origin>
              %{endfor~}
            </allowed-origins>
            <allowed-methods>
                <method>GET</method>
                <method>POST</method>
                <method>PUT</method>
                <method>DELETE</method>
                <method>OPTIONS</method>
                <method>PATCH</method>
            </allowed-methods>
            <allowed-headers>
                <header>*</header>
            </allowed-headers>
        </cors>
    </inbound>
    <backend>
        <forward-request />
    </backend>
    <outbound />
    <on-error />
  </policies>
  XML
  }
}
```

When running `terraform apply` to this config after updating to azurerm 2.7.0, we get this error

```
module.perimeter.azurerm_api_management.api-management: Modifying... [id=/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg/providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/contoso-apimgmt]
                                                                                                                                                                                      ment/service/contoso-apimgmt]
Error: creating/updating API Management Service "contoso-apimgmt" (Resource Group "rg"): apimanagement.ServiceClient#CreateOrUpdate: Failure sending request: StatusCode=400 -- Original Error: Code="NotSupported" Message="Certificate management for the default domain 'contoso-apimgmt.azure-api.net' is not allowed."         
```

Workaround is to downgrade to 2.6.0. After forcing 2.7.0 to use 2.6.0, apply is successful.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    # Locks into AzureRM 2.6.0 to work around this bug: 
    azurerm = "~>2.6.0"
  }
}
```

### Description

I like to understand why the property 'allow_nested_items_to_be_public' of a storage account is named this way. 

In every other tooling this setting is called `allowBlobPublicAccess`. So why is it that different in azurem which is not even intuitive to find. What makes it even worse is that one would not find it by searching for "blob" in the documentation because not even the description is a hint to the actual setting in azure: " (Optional) Allow or disallow nested items within this Account to opt into being public."

In additional the default is exactly the opposite as it is actually in Azure. (Default in Azure is `false` where in azurerm it is `true`)

This all makes the setting very difficult to find. Especially when there is an Azure Policy which says you the storage account cannot be created because the setting `allowBlobPublicAccess` must be set to `false` but you cannot find it in Terraform azurerm. 


Azure Portal:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c493d27-9d82-4c66-81b1-85aaf1db397e)


Azure CLI:
```bash
 az storage account create --allow-blob-public-access $false
```
ARM / Bicep:
```bicep
  properties: {
    allowBlobPublicAccess: false
  ]
```
Azure PowserShell:
```pwsh
New-AzStorageAccount -AllowBlobPublicAccess

```

Terraform azurerm:
```hcl
allow_nested_items_to_be_public = false
```

So, I think it would be worth considering if this cannot be changed to the actual name of the setting and to use the same default value as azure itself is using (false instead of true). 

Thanks!

### Description


Hello
I would like to propose a feature enhancement for the azurerm_role_assignment resource. Currently, the resource requires the use of principal_id for role assignments, which forces users to add extra code and logic in order to have a readable and maintainable configuration. By adding an optional principal_name argument, similar to how we have role_definition_id and role_definition_name, we can increase flexibility and improve code clarity.

**Motivation:**

- **Enhanced Readability**: Allowing users to reference principals by name directly simplifies the configuration and reduces the need for additional mapping logic.

- **Simplified Management**: This change would streamline role assignment declarations, particularly in environments with many role assignments.

- **Broader Impact**: The current limitation also affects Microsoft's Azure Verified Modules, as outlined in their specifications. This enhancement would align the provider with these modules and improve overall usability.

**Proposed Solution:**

- Introduce `principal_name:` Add an optional `principal_name` argument to the azurerm_role_assignment resource.
- Validation Logic: Implement validation such that either  `principal_id ` or  `principal_name ` can be provided, with a clear error if both or none are specified (or as appropriate based on design choices).
- Internal Resolution: When  `principal_name ` is provided, the provider should internally resolve it to the corresponding principal_id.

**References:**

[Terraform azurerm_role_assignment Resource Documentation](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/role_assignment#principal_id-1)
[Azure Verified Modules Role Assignments Specification](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/specs/tf/interfaces/#role-assignments)

**Additional Context:**

Currently, the lack of a principal_name argument forces users to implement additional lookup logic to derive a readable and maintainable configuration for role assignments. This feature would not only simplify our Terraform code but also bring consistency with the established patterns found in other resource arguments such as role_definition_id and role_definition_name.

I believe this enhancement would be highly beneficial for both new and existing users of the provider. Thank you for considering this request.
Thanks

      skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
      condition                              = optional(string, null)
      condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
      delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
      principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
    }))
    default     = {}
    nullable    = false
    description = <<DESCRIPTION
  A map of role assignments to create on the <RESOURCE>. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.
  
  - `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
  - `principal_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the principal to assign the role to.
  - `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
  - `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
  - `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
  - `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
  - `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
  - `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.
  
  > Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.
  DESCRIPTION
  }
  
  locals {

    condition                              = each.value.condition

Terraform crashes when you try to create an `azurerm_application_gateway` and you set the _match body_ in the _backend health probe_ to empty string `""`. Please also note, that there are other issues discussing why this terraform provider seems to think that `*` is a valid default value (#1920). Azure does *not* interpret the match body as a regex or wildcard.

- apply

~ match {
    - body        = "x" -> null
    ~ status_code = [
        - "200-399",
      ]
  }
```
Apply is successful. If you apply again, it will report the **same** change again and again. Also note, that `-> null` is wrong, it should be `-> ""`.

- Terraform version: 1.x+

The value was valid in older provider versions. It was removed during a validation tightening but the Azure API still requires/accepts it for direct ingestion scenarios. I've had to use `azapi_update_resource` as a workaround.

### Description

The resource **azurerm_network_security_rule** currently does not support the Protocols **Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP)** and **Authentication Header (AH)** for Encapsulating Security Payload IPSec traffic. As a result an ANY / ANY rule is required on the Network Security Group to allow for these protocols.

These Protocols are also known as ESP Protocol 50 and AH Protocol 51. They cannot be added as ports and must be added as protocols.

Currently the Terraform resource **azurerm_network_security_rule** has the following configurable protocols (also appears to be the same options for **azurerm_network_security_group** using the embedded **security_rule** option):

`
protocol - (Required) Network protocol this rule applies to. Possible values include Tcp, Udp, Icmp, or * (which matches all).
`

### New or Affected Resource(s)

<!--- Please list the new or affected resources and data sources. --->

azurerm_network_security_rule 
azurerm_network_security_group (security_rule)
* azurerm_v2.57.0
* Terraform v0.15.1

  location            = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name

  security_rule {
  name                        = "allow_esp_protocol"
  priority                    = 101
  direction                   = "Inbound"
  access                      = "Allow"
  protocol                    = "ESP"
  source_port_range           = "*"
  destination_port_range      = "*"
  source_address_prefix       = "*"
  destination_address_prefix  = "*"
  }

}

resource "azurerm_network_security_rule" "nsg_esp" {

  protocol                    = "ESP"

  destination_port_range      = "*"
  source_address_prefix       = "*"

  resource_group_name         = azurerm_resource_group.resourcegroup.name

resource "azurerm_network_security_rule" "nsg_ah" {

### Description of issue

This is a documentation bug.

The web page https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/data-sources/public_ip is missing the "depends_on" that is required to get the IP address of a newly created VM, see e.g. issue 310 https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/issues/310

```terraform
data "azurerm_public_ip" "example" {
  name                = azurerm_public_ip.example.name
  resource_group_name = azurerm_virtual_machine.example.resource_group_name

  # Required! Otherwise the recipe fails if the IP address is not already created on Azure
  depends_on = [azurerm_virtual_machine.example]

## Summary

When `azurerm_static_web_app` creates a Static Web App via the ARM API, Azure sets
`provider: None` on the resource. This silently breaks two things:

- **Managed Functions do not deploy** — the GitHub Actions build pipeline errors and
  no deploy token is issued.
- **GitHub integration is absent** — no deploy webhook is created, no GitHub App is
  installed on the repository.

This is not a bug in the provider itself (the ARM API simply does not support the
GitHub App registration flow), but it is a significant undocumented footgun that
causes real debugging time for users.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Static Web App using `azurerm_static_web_app` with any configuration.
2. Attempt to deploy an Azure Functions API alongside the frontend via GitHub Actions
   using the `Azure/static-web-apps-deploy` action.
3. The deployment pipeline errors — no deploy token is available and managed Functions
   are not reachable.

## Expected behavior (docs)

The resource documentation should include a note explaining:

- The ARM API creates SWAs with `provider: None`, which disables GitHub integration
  and managed Functions.
- The workaround is to create the SWA using `az staticwebapp create --source` (which
  performs the full GitHub App registration and sets `provider: GitHub`), then import
  it into Terraform state with `terraform import`.
- After import, `terraform apply` can be used normally for all subsequent configuration
  and app settings updates — only the initial creation requires `az`.

## Workaround

```bash
# 1. Create the SWA with full GitHub integration via az CLI
az staticwebapp create \
  --name <swa-name> \
  --resource-group <rg-name> \
  --location <location> \
  --source <github-repo-url> \
  --branch <branch> \
  --login-with-github

# 2. Import into Terraform state
terraform import azurerm_static_web_app.app /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.Web/staticSites/<name>

# 3. Use terraform apply normally from here for settings/config updates
```

## References

- Azure docs acknowledge `az staticwebapp create` as the path for GitHub integration
- The `azurerm_static_web_app` resource page currently has no mention of this limitation

### Terraform Version

1.x

### AzureRM Provider Version

3.117.1

### Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_storage_account

### Description

This is a follow-up to the locked issue #24793. The issue still affects users trying to **import existing BlockBlobStorage accounts** into Terraform state, even with azurerm provider v3.117.1.

The suggested workaround in #24793 (patching Azure to set `accessTier: null`) requires manual intervention and doesn't address the root cause in the provider.

### Test Environment
- **Terraform**: 1.x
- **azurerm provider**: 3.117.1
- **Storage Account**: BlockBlobStorage, Premium_LRS, HNS enabled
- **Azure Region**: germanywestcentral

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an existing BlockBlobStorage account in Azure that has `accessTier: "Hot"` set (visible in Azure Portal and API response)

2. Create Terraform resource definition (without `access_tier` attribute since provider says it's not valid):
```hcl
resource "azurerm_storage_account" "example" {
  name                     = "exampleblockblobaccount"
  resource_group_name      = "example-rg"
  location                 = "germanywestcentral"
  account_tier             = "Premium"
  account_replication_type = "LRS"
  account_kind             = "BlockBlobStorage"
  # access_tier omitted - provider says not valid for BlockBlobStorage
  is_hns_enabled           = true
  # ... other attributes
}
```

3. Run `terraform import`:
```
terraform import azurerm_storage_account.example "/subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/<account-name>"
```
   **Result**: ✅ Import succeeds

4. Run `terraform plan`:
```
terraform plan
```
   **Result**: ❌ **Fails with error:**
```
Error: 1 error occurred:
      * `access_tier` is only available for accounts where `kind` is set to one of: BlobStorage / FileStorage / StorageV2

  with azurerm_storage_account.example,
```

### Root Cause

The Azure API returns `"accessTier": "Hot"` for BlockBlobStorage accounts. The provider:
1. Reads this value during import/refresh and stores it in state
2. Then fails its own validation because `access_tier` is "not valid for BlockBlobStorage"

This is a circular validation problem - the provider rejects a value that Azure itself returns.

### Why the Workaround is Insufficient

The suggested workaround (patching Azure to set `accessTier: null`) works, but:
1. Requires manual intervention outside of Terraform for each affected storage account
2. Users importing existing infrastructure shouldn't need to modify Azure resources first
3. The provider should handle this gracefully by ignoring `access_tier` for BlockBlobStorage during read/refresh

### Suggested Fix

During `Read` operations for storage accounts with `account_kind = "BlockBlobStorage"`, the provider should either:
1. Not read/store the `accessTier` value from Azure, OR
2. Skip validation of `access_tier` for BlockBlobStorage accounts

This would allow seamless import of existing BlockBlobStorage accounts without manual intervention.

### Expected Behaviour

Initial apply works correctly - the NSG and inline rules are created as per var.nsgs.

If a rule is deleted from var.nsgs security_rules, for example "rule3", terraform plan/apply should show the **only change** being the _deletion of rule3_.

This behavior should be consistent irrespective of whether any of the rules contain properties with lists (e.g. "source_address_prefixes"), dynamic lookups, or basic strings.



### Actual Behaviour


After the initial apply/deployment succeeds, If "rule3" is removed from the security_rules section of var.nsgs, and plan or apply run subsequently, plan shows rules other than "rule3" being deleted and re-created. Specifically, in the example provided, deleting rule3 from security_rules after initial apply, and doing a second plan/apply, shows "rule4" and "rule6" being deleted and re-created, but not rule5.

From my testing this only happens when the list of security_rules contains rules with fields of type list(string) e.g. "source_address_prefixes" and "destination_address_prefixes" in the examples above.

If the rules in var.nsgs contain only simple string-based properties (no properties with data type = list(string), any rule in the list can be removed, and plan or apply correctly shows just that rule being removed as would be expected.



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Remove "rule3" from the security_rules section of _variable "nsgs"_
2. Re-run terraform plan or apply
3. Observe the plan output showing "rule4" and "rule6" being deleted and recreated (not expected) alongside the deletion of rule3 (expected)
This makes reviewing the plan problematic especially in scenarios where they may be a large number of rules, and does not inspire confidence because valid rules appear to be deleted.
4. Re-test by doing a TF destroy, changing the list of security_rules to remove any list-based fields, apply, remove a rule in the middle of the list again, plan/apply and observe the plan output show just the rule being deleted.

Have I produced this issue through coding, or is it a known issue or bug?


### Important Factoids

In this instance azurerm_network_security_rule is not a viable alternative because is does not track drift in rules created on an NSG outside of the terraform deployment, and that breaks compliance.

_This issue was originally opened by @terryjoycenhs as hashicorp/terraform#19722. It was migrated here as a result of the [provider split](https://www.hashicorp.com/blog/upcoming-provider-changes-in-terraform-0-10/). The original body of the issue is below._

<hr>

```
Terraform v0.11.11
+ provider.azurerm v1.18.0
```

### Terraform Configuration Files
<!--
Paste the relevant parts of your Terraform configuration between the ``` marks below.

For large Terraform configs, please use a service like Dropbox and share a link to the ZIP file. For security, you can also encrypt the files using our GPG public key.
-->

```
resource "azurerm_subnet" "edge" {
  name                      = "111-${var.locale-short}-edge-${var.environment}"
  resource_group_name       = "${azurerm_resource_group.main.name}"
  virtual_network_name      = "${azurerm_virtual_network.main.name}"
  address_prefix            = "172.${var.address-middle}.${var.edge-address-end}"
}
```
```
resource "azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association" "edge" {
  subnet_id                 = "${azurerm_subnet.edge.id}"
  network_security_group_id = "${azurerm_network_security_group.nsg-edge.id}"
}
```

### Expected Behavior

That the network security group assignment is kept between applys.

### Actual Behavior
<!--
What happens is that the network security group is assigned to the network subnet and on the next apply it is removed.  It is then applied again on the next apply and removed again after and so on.  
-->

### Steps to Reproduce

To reproduce this I keep running the apply commands.  Which produces this in the summary.
```
+ azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association.edge
      id:                                      <computed>
      network_security_group_id:               "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/111-ukw-staging/providers/Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/nsg-ukw-edge-staging"
      subnet_id:                               "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/111-ukw-staging/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/111-ukw-vnet/subnets/111-ukw-edge-staging"
```
Then on the following run will do this.
```
~ azurerm_subnet.edge
      network_security_group_id:               "/subscriptions/xxx/resourceGroups/111-ukw-staging/providers/Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/nsg-ukw-edge-staging" => ""
```
This is then reflected in Azure when run. 

To stop this from happening I need to add back into the network creation the line 
```
  network_security_group_id = "${azurerm_network_security_group.nsg-edge.id}"
```

### AzureRM Provider Version

3.110.0 (current v5.0.0 source appears unchanged for this path)

### Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_maintenance_configuration

### Affected Location(s)

Australia East (time_zone = "AUS Eastern Standard Time")

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl

    azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"

  resource_group_name = "example-resource-group"
  location            = "australiaeast"
  scope               = "InGuestPatch"

  in_guest_user_patch_mode = "User"

  window {
    start_date_time = "2025-10-05 02:00"
    duration        = "03:00"
    time_zone       = "AUS Eastern Standard Time"
    recur_every     = "Day"
  }

  install_patches {
    reboot = "IfRequired"

    windows {
      classifications_to_include = ["Critical", "Security"]
    }
  }
}


`2025-10-05 02:00` is a nonexistent local time in this Windows time zone because clocks advance directly from 02:00 to 03:00. For a future equivalent test, use `2026-10-04 02:15`.
```

### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Error: creating Maintenance Configuration
(Subscription: "<redacted>"
Resource Group Name: "<redacted>"
Maintenance Configuration Name: "<redacted>"):
Put "https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/<redacted>/resourceGroups/<redacted>/providers/Microsoft.Maintenance/maintenanceConfigurations/<redacted>?api-version=2023-04-01": context deadline exceeded

with azurerm_maintenance_configuration.example,
on main.tf line 1, in resource "azurerm_maintenance_configuration" "example":
resource "azurerm_maintenance_configuration" "example" {


The request remained pending until the provider's default 30-minute create timeout. The Azure Activity Log recorded `InternalServerError` for `Create or update maintenance configuration`.
```

### Expected Behaviour

The provider should detect that the combination of `start_date_time` and `time_zone` represents a nonexistent local time and return a clear validation error before issuing the Azure request. At minimum, the operation should fail promptly with an actionable `InvalidMaintenanceWindow` response rather than waiting for the full create timeout.

The provider should not silently choose a replacement time unless that normalization is explicitly documented.

### Actual Behaviour

The AzureRM provider passes the nonexistent local timestamp to the `Microsoft.Maintenance/maintenanceConfigurations` `2023-04-01` API. The PUT remains pending and Terraform fails after 30 minutes with `context deadline exceeded`; Azure Activity Log records `InternalServerError`.

Comparative testing isolated the DST-gap timestamp:

- Renaming the maintenance configuration: failed.
- Deleting and recreating it: still failed with the DST-gap start time.
- Changing only the duration: failed.
- Changing `start_date_time` to `03:15`: succeeded.
- Other maintenance configurations in the same Terraform run succeeded.

Microsoft Support reproduced that Azure Portal and Azure PowerShell normalize a timestamp in the skipped period, while valid times such as `01:45` and `03:15` are accepted unchanged. They recommended using a time outside the DST transition and reporting the Terraform behavior.

Source inspection shows v5.0.0 still uses the `2023-04-01` Maintenance API, retains a 30-minute create timeout, and does not validate `start_date_time` against `time_zone`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `azurerm_maintenance_configuration` with `time_zone = "AUS Eastern Standard Time"`.
2. Set `start_date_time` to a nonexistent Sydney DST-transition time. The original observed value was `2025-10-05 02:00`; the next future equivalent is `2026-10-04 02:15`.
3. Run `terraform apply`.
4. Observe that the create operation waits until the 30-minute context deadline.
5. Change only the start time to `03:15` on the same date and run `terraform apply` again.
6. Observe that creation succeeds.

### Important Factoids

This occurred in a standard public Azure subscription using the Australia East region and Windows time zone `AUS Eastern Standard Time`.  The original runtime reproduction used AzureRM v3.110.0. AzureRM v5.0.0 was not deployed in the affected production environment, but its current resource implementation still imports `maintenance/2023-04-01/maintenanceconfigurations`, passes `start_date_time` through unchanged, and retains the same 30-minute timeout.  A raw REST reproduction has not yet been completed, so ownership may be shared with or ultimately belong to the Microsoft.Maintenance service. Client-side validation would nevertheless prevent the unhelpful 30-minute timeout.

- Current resource implementation: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v5.0.0/internal/services/maintenance/maintenance_configuration_resource.go
- Original provider implementation: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/v3.110.0/internal/services/maintenance/maintenance_configuration_resource.go
- Microsoft Maintenance REST API: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/maintenance/maintenance-configurations/create-or-update?view=rest-maintenance-2023-09-01-preview
- Microsoft API version change log: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.maintenance/change-log/maintenanceconfigurations

```hcl
  ~ resource "azurerm_linux_virtual_machine" "instance" {

### Expected Behaviour

When Terraform inspects an existing subnet with service endpoints and the service endpoints are not declared in the same order as described in the Terraform resource, the resource is not updated. Terraform should evaluate the list of service endpoints and ensure the list contains the desired values (in any order).

Service endpoint triggered updates should only occur when the list of service endpoints differs in contents (not by the ordering of contents).

### Actual Behaviour

When Terraform inspects an existing subnet with service endpoints and the service endpoints are all present, but declared in a different order, an update-in-place is triggered. The update finishes, but the service endpoints are not re-ordered by Azure because the ordering doesn't matter.

As a result, during the next plan/apply the subnet is updated again. This continues until:
1. the Terraform file lists the subnets in the exact order as reflected in the Azure resource definition OR
2. a service endpoint is added/removed which triggers an actual update to the Azure resource and re-orders the service endpoints during the update

4. Import the resource to start tracking it in terraform state
5. `terraform plan` will show the resource needs updated
6. `terraform apply` will attempt to change the resource
7. `terraform plan` again will show the resource needs updated
8. Re-order the service endpoints in the Terraform file
9. `terraform plan` no longer shows an update is needed

### Important Factoids

The `azurerm_virtual_machine`resource supports data_disks, but this isn't possible with the new `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine` or `azurerm_windows_virtual_machine`.

[edit]

As soon as the vm is created, the `cloud-init` initialization starts. As we can not attach a data disk in a single operation with `azurerm_linux_virtual_machine`, **we can not mount nor do anything with the data disk** during the `cloud-init` operation. 

However, it's pretty common (a best practice) to 
- use cloud-init for vm initialization
- rely on a data disk for persistent data

👉 **This use case is not possible anymore.** 😢

### Description

`azurerm_key_vault_secret` requires read permission to the secret value. This is a security problem because it breaks it impossible to reference a secret and assign it to another resource without reading the secret value to the client.

I think there should be two data resources: `azurerm_key_vault_secret` and `azurerm_key_vault_secret_value`. The first one should only reference the secret, but not read the value. ### Description

It would be useful if the data source for `azurerm_user_assigned_identity` could support using a resource ID, object ID, or other. The data source for `azuread_service_principal` supports a number of invocations.

The example use-case here is needing to create the identity before using it in a data source. I'm using the data source in a module, and the only way to pass this in is via the `name` and `resource_group` fields. These are not determined after creation, so if creating a `azurerm_user_assigned_identity` resource and passing the `name` into a module where a data source for `azurerm_user_assigned_identity` is used, it creates a race condition. The `name` is known so there is no dependency on creating the `azurerm_user_assigned_identity` resource before passing the `name` to the module.

When using this in a virtual machine or scale set, this results in an error like the following:

  85:     identity_ids = [data.azurerm_user_assigned_identity.consul.id]

Null values are not allowed for this attribute value.

The major difference I see is that the service principal appears to have it's dashes removed in the azurerm_role_assignment error (`xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx`), while the az command has the dashes (`xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`).

### Expected Behaviour

The expected behavior is for Terraform to simply update the existing resource without replacement. The Azure rest API allows for modification of this setting without replacement. I will also add that the current behavior of this module makes adopting this setting for existing subnets with large amounts of resources on them extremely challenging.

### Actual Behaviour

As seen in the plan, terraform wants to replace the subnet specifically because of the change of `default_outbound_access_enabled` from true to false.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create a subnet with `default_outbound_access_enabled` set to true, deploy it, and then switch it to false and run a plan.

### Debug Output/Panic Output

```shell
Error: retrieving Storage Account (Subscription: "<redacted>"
Resource Group Name: "prod10"
Storage Account Name: "tlprod10eckcluster"): unexpected status 400 (400 Bad Request) with error:
NoRegisteredProviderFound: No registered resource provider found for location 'chinanorth3' and API version '2025-08-01' for type 'storageAccounts'.
The supported api-versions are '... 2025-06-01, 2025-01-01, ...'
```

### Expected Behaviour

Provider should use a Storage API version supported in Azure China cloud (for chinanorth3), or gracefully fall back to a supported version, so plan/refresh succeeds.



### Actual Behaviour

Provider uses 2025-08-01 for Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts operations, and Azure China rejects it with NoRegisteredProviderFound (HTTP 400), causing plan failure.



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Azure China cloud (environment = "china"), region chinanorth3.
2. Use hashicorp/azurerm provider v4.71.0.
3. Run terraform init && terraform plan with a azurerm_storage_account resource (or refresh existing one).
4. Observe NoRegisteredProviderFound for API version 2025-08-01.
5. Pin provider to v4.70.0 and rerun; plan succeeds (workaround).

### Important Factoids

Environment: Azure China (Mooncake), not public Azure. Region: chinanorth3. Regression window: issue appears on v4.71.0; workaround is pinning < 4.71.0 (tested with 4.70.0).

### Description
Good morning,

We have an infrastructure generated in Azure which we are trying to terraform. 
In particular, we have a problem with admin_ssh_key "public_key" in "azurerm_linux_virtual_machine" when the key imported is in the following format:
*---- BEGIN SSH2 PUBLIC KEY ----
Comment: "rsa-key-20200715"
ssh-rsa AAA....
---- END SSH2 PUBLIC KEY --*

We have several virtual machines with their linked ssh key in different format and we reference to them using the *file* function:

admin_ssh_key {
username = "azureuser"
public_key = file(<path_to_ssh_key>)
}

After performing the command terraform plan, it manages to compare information with keys in string format but not in the ---- BEGIN SSH2 PUBLIC KEY ---- format.

I tried using file either with or without .pub extension but I didn't get any result. 
Below a screenshot of the error:
![decoding_error](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9596482/104442902-060e7c00-5596-11eb-9dbd-700f150855e6.PNG)

I also tried using an input key even in the ssh-rsa common format (ignoring the 'BEGIN/END' and 'comment' keyword) but Terraform tries to forces replacement in this case.

3. run terraform plan/apply

### Terraform (and AzureRM Provider) Version

<!-- this can be obtained from `terraform -v` -->

```
Terraform v1.0.6
on linux_amd64
+ provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/azurerm v2.75.0
```

### Terraform Configuration Files

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

```hcl
resource "azurerm_subscription" "dev" {
  alias             = "dev"
  subscription_name = "Dev"
  subscription_id   = "e42c1859-1c46-4c0b-a52c-36d09f272ac2"
}

resource "azurerm_management_group_subscription_association" "dev" {
  subscription_id     = azurerm_subscription.dev.subscription_id
  management_group_id = azurerm_management_group.dev.id
}
```

Trying to apply the above produces the error:

```
│ Error: "subscription_id" expected to be valid subscription ID, got "e42c1859-1c46-4c0b-a52c-36d09f272ac2"
│ 
│   with azurerm_management_group_subscription_association.dev,
│   on subscriptions.tf line 19, in resource "azurerm_management_group_subscription_association" "dev":
│   19:   subscription_id     = azurerm_subscription.dev.subscription_id
│ 
╵
```

Additionally, trying to use the `.id` property instead  of `.subscription_id` gives a similar error:

```
Error: "subscription_id" expected to be valid subscription ID, got "/providers/Microsoft.Subscription/aliases/dev"
```

### Description / Feedback

Scenario: Subscriptions existed pre-terraform, and the subscriptions were brought into terraform using the methodology described under [Adding an alias to an existing subscription](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/subscription#example-usage---adding-an-alias-to-an-existing-subscription)

The `azurerm_management_group_subscription_association` resource expects the `subscription_id` to be in the format `/subscriptions/{subscriptionid}` and there isn't a direct attribute output from the `azurerm_subscription` resource that matches this.

 This is further confused by the terraform example in the documentation, which using the data provider for `azurerm_subscription` which shows this same approach, just using a `data.azurerm_subscription` block instead of a resource `azurerm_subscription` block. 

```hcl
data "azurerm_management_group" "example" {
  name = "exampleManagementGroup"
}

data "azurerm_subscription" "example" {
  subscription_id = "12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012"
}

resource "azurerm_management_group_subscription_association" "example" {
  management_group_id = data.azurerm_management_group.example.id
  subscription_id     = data.azurerm_subscription.example.id
}
```

I would expect the data block to behave similarly to the resource block. I would also expect that the `azurerm_management_group_subscription_association` resource would accept `subscription_id` in a simple uuid format (typical convention used in many other parts of this resource provider) so it can be directly referenced by a managed subscription in terraform.

### Workaround

Format the `subscription_id` directly like the provider expects:

```hcl
resource "azurerm_subscription" "dev" {
  alias             = "dev"
  subscription_name = "Dev"
  subscription_id   = "e42c1859-1c46-4c0b-a52c-36d09f272ac2"
}

resource "azurerm_management_group_subscription_association" "dev" {
  subscription_id     = "/subscriptions/${azurerm_subscription.dev.subscription_id}"
  management_group_id = azurerm_management_group.dev.id
}
```

### Description

<!--- Please leave a helpful description of the feature request here. --->
When implementating a Terraform module, you may have to support inputs given as datasources or terraform references. The fact that the [`azurerm_virtual_network`](https://www.terraform.io/docs/providers/azurerm/d/virtual_network.html#attributes-reference) datasource doesn't include the `resource_group_name` the resource [`azurerm_virtual_network`](https://www.terraform.io/docs/providers/azurerm/r/virtual_network.html#attributes-reference) exports makes it difficult to have a lean and common module interface for both kind of inputs.

### New or Affected Resource(s)

<!--- Please list the new or affected resources and data sources. --->

* data.azurerm_virtual_network

### Potential Terraform Configuration

<!--- Information about code formatting: https://help.github.com/articles/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax/#quoting-code --->

```hcl
module "mymodule" {
  ...
  peerings = [ { vnet = data.azurerm_virtual_network.vnet_datasource, resource_group_name = "need-to-be-provided" },
               { vnet = azurerm_virtual_network.vnet_in_current_tf_state, resource_group_name = azurerm_virtual_network.vnet_in_current_tf_state.resource_group_name }]
}
```

In the former case, you have to explicitely pass the resource_group_name as it can't be inferred by the datasource, in the latter you can use the exported attribute of the vnet resource. 
IMHO both should provide the same attributes.

### Expected Behaviour

The provider should save the resource into state but recognize it's not in the state it expects so that subsequent plans or applies can attempt to fix the problem.

If you pass in malformed `additional_unattend_content` to the resource you can trigger the error.

The problem is that the resource **IS CREATED**, but it does hit an internal provision error, however the resource still exists, in this case the provider should 100% record the resource into state but mark it as in a bad condition so subsequent plans and runs work.

In this case the provider is not behaving properly, regardless of the error from Azure, it should be recorded into state.

The other underlying issue here is that the provider just exits upon this error `OSProvisioningInternalError` but it shouldn't, worse case it should retry for a defined timeout period, then exit safely and record everything it knows into state.

### Actual Behaviour

The resource isn't included in state at all but the resource exists in Azure.

Pass in malformed `additional_unattend_content`

# Summary:

  Azure Kubernetes (AKS) manages it's own resources, outside of the view of terraform.
  When AKS is deployed, it registers itself with an Azure Private DNS zone, this registration is out of the view of terraform.

```
resource "azurerm_private_dns_zone" "privatedns" {
  name                = "privatelink.eastus2.azmk8s.io"
  resource_group_name = local.aks_resource_group

    lifecycle {

      tags
    ]

### Expected Behaviour

Terraform applies the custom domain with indirect CNAME validation enabled, and the same should be reflected in the TFSTATE file (i.e corresponding parameter `use_subdomain` should be set to true in TFSTATE). ### Actual Behaviour

The observed behaviour only partially matches the expected behaviour. `terraform apply` completes without any error, so it seems TF is able to configure a custom domain in the storage account with the 'Indirect CNAME validation' option enabled (the custom domain specified in the configuration is visible on the Portal as well, under Networking/Custom Domain). ```shell
Resource Group Name: "customer-dnszones"): unexpected status 403 (403 Forbidden) with error: AuthorizationFailed: The client '267b0905-1091-4b0a-87c9-dadc7c5c56a2' with object id '267b0905-1091-4b0a-87c9-dadc7c5c56a2' does not have authorization to perform action 'Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/read' over scope '/subscriptions/566f2f89-58cd-4d39-a602-60ddbc6e8d14/resourceGroups/customer-dnszones' or the scope is invalid. ### Expected Behaviour

Most customers we work with have DNS zones in a central subscription and service principals are given access to the zones the deployment requires.
The customer has provided the service principal with the Private DNS Zone Contributor role to the zone. 
This should be enough for Terraform to manage resources within the zone.
azurerm provider v3.77.0 does not produce the error as it must obtain the zone details via other methods.
We should not need to ask a customer for read access over a whole resource group to perform a task that should not require that access.

### Actual Behaviour

The private dns zones details are returned without requiring resource group reader.

### Steps to Reproduce

Give your SP the Private DNS Zone Contributor role to the zone and then run TF plan/apply.
The error appears on apply.

### Debug Output

(after the ***second*** `terraform apply`)
```
Terraform will perform the following actions:

  # azurerm_storage_account.storage_account will be updated in-place
  ~ resource "azurerm_storage_account" "storage_account" {
      + access_tier                       = "Hot"
        id                                = "/subscriptions/<subscriptionid>/resourceGroups/testingstorage/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/testingstorage"
        name                              = "testingstorage"
        # (26 unchanged attributes hidden)


        # (2 unchanged blocks hidden)
    }

Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
```

### Expected Behaviour

For `account_tier = "Premium"` and `account_kind = "BlockBlobStorage"` the field `access_tier` should not have any effect (since only `Hot` is allowed and the provider defaults to this value). Successive calls to `terraform apply` with the same configuration should not show any changes.

### Actual Behaviour

When (re-)applying this configuration on an existing storage account, the provider keeps reporting that it will add `access_tier = "Hot"` to the resource state. However, this is never done and the next call will yield the same message.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform apply` on the file posted above
2. A second `terraform apply` on the exact same file without changing anything

### Workaround

As a simple workaround you can add
```hcl
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [
      access_tier
    ]
  }
```

### Additional information

We observed this behavior since some point between the 17th and 18th of January (without having changed anything in our infrastructure). This might perhaps be related to an upstream change in the Azure API, but I didn't find any official changelogs. I just noticed that `az storage account show` doesn't show this field either, so perhaps they have silently removed this field (which only applies to kinds `BlobStorage`, `FileStorage` and `StorageV2` after all).

### Description

Per this [link](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-during-vm-creation#azure-backup-resource-group-for-virtual-machines) you can configure recovery vault backup policies to create the restore point collection in a named resource group (this will then be created automatically the first time the backup policy is used to back up something like a VM).

I currently use a cli (bash) script in a local-exec provisioner to check the prefix/suffix settings and set it correctly if it's misconfigured. Having this set in terraform would remove the need to manually manage this setting. The default name for this resource group is **AzureBackupRG_{region}_1** e.g. **AzureBackupRG_uksouth_1**. Support Attaching multiple Disks azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment 



### Description
Requesting enhancement for azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment to support attaching multiple data disk to a VM.
Current implementation attaches 1 disk at a time. With Windows VM, this process becomes very slow when say more than 1 disk is required to be attached. As after every disk attach, VM update is called. Once VM update is done, only then the next disk is attached and again VM Update is called.

VM update, considerable, slows down the process.

Suggestion is to allow attaching multiple disk and then run VM update only once.


### New or Affected Resource(s)
* azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment

### Potential Terraform Configuration
```
 resource "azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment" "attach_disk" {   
  depends_on         = ["azurerm_virtual_machine.vm"]
  managed_disk_ids    = "${azurerm_managed_disk.md.*.id}"
  virtual_machine_id = "${local.vm_id}"
  lun                = ["0","",""]    # or autoincrement lun from the first number provided
  caching            = "ReadWrite"
}
```

### Current Terraform Implementation
```
resource "azurerm_virtual_machine_data_disk_attachment" "attach_disk" {
  depends_on         = ["azurerm_virtual_machine.vm"]
  count              =      "${var.disks_per_vm}"
  managed_disk_id    = "${element(azurerm_managed_disk.md.*.id, count.index)}"
  virtual_machine_id = "${local.vm_id}"
  lun                = "${count.index%var.disks_per_vm}"
  caching            = "ReadWrite"
}
```

During the creation of the storage account, don't call queue properties before private endpoints are created.

So we would have to put a rule *.queue.core.windows.net in our firewall to allow the creation of new storage accounts (as we don't know all the storage account names that will be created in the future, but of course this is not desired).

### Expected Behavior
The vm extensions should wait until the vm is successfully deployed before attempting to deploy

### Actual Behavior
The extensions attempt to deploy before the vm is done so they fail.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. `terraform plan`
2. `terraform apply`
3. Watching the cli shows that the extensions are deployed before the vm is completely deployed which causes them to fail.

### Important Factoids
Because count is being used to deploy multiple vm's, I can not use interpolations within the depends_on property to force the vm extension to wait until the corresponding vm is deployed.

Furthermore, the vm extension that is deployed on machine 1 needs to complete successfully before moving on to machine 2 because it relies on machine 1 being done or it will fail.

I believe that having the ability to use interpolations within the depends_on property would solve this sort of issue.

However, it does not appear to be possible to migrate to use the ephemeral capabilities without terraform regenerating the secret. A typical starting point before ephemeral would be

````
resource "random_password" "random" {
  length           = 8
}

resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "secret" {
  name             = "randomsecret"
  value            = random_password.random.result
  key_vault_id     = azurerm_key_vault.sbox_keyvault.id
  content_type     = "test"
}
````

and I am looking to change to something like this

````
ephemeral "random_password" "random" {
  length           = 8
}

resource "random_integer" "taint_to_generate_new_password" {
  min = 13
  max = 1000003
}

resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "secret" {
  name             = "randomsecret"
  value_wo         = ephemeral_random_password.random.result
  value_wo_version = random_integer.taint_to_generate_new_password.result
  key_vault_id     = azurerm_key_vault.sbox_keyvault.id
  content_type     = "test"
}
````
(If anyone has any better idea on how to manage the version please let me know, but that isn't the point of this issue.)

This wants to destroy the original random_password resource, which is fair enough, we changed to ephemeral so it should be removed from state. It also wants to recreate keyvault secret because value_wo_version has changed:

````  # azurerm_key_vault_secret.secret will be updated in-place
  ~ resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "secret" {
        id                      = "redacted"
        name                    = "randomsecret"
        tags                    = {}
      - value                   = (sensitive value) -> null
      ~ value_wo_version        = 0 -> (known after apply)
        # (7 unchanged attributes hidden)
    }
````
I cannot change all of the secrets. The knock on effect would be huge. But as the value_wo_version is zero (this is the default/never been set value) we should be able to set our generated version to 0 (despite the min being 13 the is still possible) and all would be good..
````
terraform import random_integer.taint_to_generate_new_password "0,13,1000003"
````
However, now the plan is:
````
  # random_password.random will be destroyed
  # (because random_password.random is not in configuration)
  - resource "random_password" "random" {
      - bcrypt_hash = (sensitive value) -> null
      - id          = "none" -> null
      - length      = 8 -> null
      - lower       = true -> null
      - min_lower   = 0 -> null
      - min_numeric = 0 -> null
      - min_special = 0 -> null
      - min_upper   = 0 -> null
      - number      = true -> null
      - numeric     = true -> null
      - result      = (sensitive value) -> null
      - special     = true -> null
      - upper       = true -> null
    }

Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.
╷
│ Error: expected value_wo_version to be at least (1), got 0
│
│   with azurerm_key_vault_secret.secret,
│   on keyvaultsecret.tf line 13, in resource "azurerm_key_vault_secret" "secret":
│   13:   value_wo_version = random_integer.taint_to_generate_new_password.result
│
````
I did a quick play with the provider allowing zero to be set but this was not quite so simple as it sounded. There is a reason why the min value is 1, and I have run out of time to look any deeper at the moment. Hoping someone can help with ideas or alternatives!

azurerm_key_vault_secret timesout at about 2 minutes by default during recovery.

When trying to create a secret or key in key vault, if the key/secret already exists terraform recovers that. ### Expected Behaviour

API is updated as expected.

### Actual Behaviour

API is not updated, and the following error is shown:
```
╷
│ Error: creating/updating Api (Subscription: 
│ Resource Group Name: "my-rg"
│ Service Name: "my-apim"
│ Api: "testapi;rev=1"): performing CreateOrUpdate: unexpected status 400 (400 Bad Request) with error: ValidationError: Cannot use OAuth2AuthenticationSettings in combination with OAuth2 nor openid.
│ 
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `terraform apply` to create the api (wich works)
2. Make a change on the api. For example, add an operation to the openapi.yaml, add a description.
3. Run `terraform apply` again to update the api. 
4. Error is shown and api is not correctly updated.

### Important Factoids

The main problem seems to be that the `authenticationSettings` property is different (wrong) when the API is updated. 

When the API is created initially the `authenticationSettings` properties seems to be correct, like:
```json
        "authenticationSettings": {
            "oAuth2": {
                "authorizationServerId": "myauthserver",
                "scope": ""
            }
        },

```

But for the update the `authenticationSettings` properties contains duplicated values (`oAuth` and `oAuth2AuthenticationSettings`) which are not valid and the Azure API responses therefore with HTTP 400:

```json
        "authenticationSettings": {
            "oAuth2": {
                "authorizationServerId": "myauthserver",
                "scope": ""
            },
            "oAuth2AuthenticationSettings": [
                {
                    "authorizationServerId": "myauthserver",
                    "scope": ""
                }
            ],
            "openidAuthenticationSettings": []
        },
```

Not sure, but maybe the version 4.22.0 uses a newer Azure API version? 
It seems that the duplication of the settings happens already at the Azure API when doing a GET. With API Version `2022-08-01` the API seems to return `oAuth2` and `oAuth2AuthenticationSettings` and when using the same values in the PUT the error happens.
But with API-Version `2021-08-01` only the `oAuth2` is included in the response of a GET request and reusing the body, as it was returned, work, therefore. But with the API-Version `2022-08-01` either `oAuth2` or `oAuth2AuthenticationSettings` needs to be removed for the PUT request (otherwise the error happens).  
So, it seems also be a bug on the Azure API but can be worked around by correcting the body before using it again in the PUT request.

### Description

Currently, the azurerm_resource_group resource in the Azure provider for Terraform can only create resource groups within the subscription specified in the default provider configuration or a statically declared provider with an alias. This limitation makes it challenging to dynamically manage scenarios where both a subscription and its resource groups are created in the same Terraform plan.

To address this, I propose adding a new argument, subscription_id, to the azurerm_resource_group resource. This argument would allow users to explicitly specify the subscription in which the resource group should be created. The value for subscription_id could be dynamically referenced from other resources, such as the azurerm_subscription resource.

**Use Case:**

A common use case is dynamically creating a new subscription and immediately provisioning a resource group within that subscription. Currently, users must:

1. Create the subscription.
2. Manually configure or statically define a new provider with the subscription's ID.
3. Reference the provider using the provider argument in azurerm_resource_group.

This process adds unnecessary complexity and limits flexibility in automation workflows.

### New or Affected Resource(s)/Data Source(s)

azurerm_resource_group

### Potential Terraform Configuration

```hcl
Add an optional subscription_id argument to the azurerm_resource_group resource. If this argument is provided, the resource group will be created in the specified subscription. This eliminates the need for manually defining multiple providers for each subscription.

resource "azurerm_subscription" "example" {
  display_name = "Example Subscription"
  billing_scope_id = "<billing_scope_id>"
}

resource "azurerm_resource_group" "example" {
  name     = "example-rg"
  location = "East US"

  subscription_id = azurerm_subscription.example.subscription_id
}
```

azurerm_public_ip domain_name_label incorrectly limited to 61 chars

Azure provider limits domain name labels to <= 61 chars
The RFC1035 says domain name labels must be <= 63 chars
Azure is allowing domain name labels of at least 64 chars

provider.azurerm v1.16.0

   resource_group_name = "rg-prod-cus-compute"

   sku = "Basic" 
   domain_name_label = "cust-c-u-s-0-x-x-x-x-x-x-x-f7ecdfea-993c-43bf-9d21-36af0a67a8d2"

    showback = "Compute"

}

### Debug Output

N/A

### Panic Output

N/A

### Expected Behavior

terraform plan should be successful

### Actual Behavior
```
terraform plan

Error: azurerm_public_ip.rg-prod-cus-compute__aadds-f7ecdfea993c43bf9d2136af0a67a8d2-pip: "domain_name_label" cannot be longer than 61 characters: "cust-c-u-s-0-x-x-x-x-x-x-x-f7ecdfea-993c-43bf-9d21-36af0a67a8d2"
```
### Steps to Reproduce

Create a public IP resource with domain_name_label that is 62-63 chars long and run `terraform plan`

### Important Factoids

- Azure provider limits domain name labels to <= 61 chars
- The RFC1035 says domain name labels must be <= 63 chars
- Azure is allowing domain name labels of at least 64 chars


### References

[RFC1035 section 2.3.1](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1035) says "Labels must be 63 characters or less."

[resource_arm_public_ip.go](https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-azurerm/blob/master/azurerm/resource_arm_public_ip.go) line 289 limits label name to 61 chars
```go
	if len(value) > 61 {
		errors = append(errors, fmt.Errorf(
			"%q cannot be longer than 61 characters: %q", k, value))
	}
```

Azure is allowing domain_name_labels with 64 chars: 
```bash
$ az network public-ip list -g rg-prod-cus-compute | jq .[].dnsSettings.domainNameLabel | sed s/\"//g 
cust-c-u-s-0-x-x-x-x-x-x-x-f7ecdfea-993c-43bf-9d21-36af0a67a8d2

$ az network public-ip list -g rg-prod-cus-compute | jq .[].dnsSettings.domainNameLabel | sed s/\"//g | wc -c
64
```

### Expected Behaviour

This is supposed to deploy an APIM and a Custom Domain Gateway. 

### Actual Behaviour

It is working fine and deploy an APIM and a Custom Domain Gateway.

But on each apply after the first deployment terraform try to edit the Custom Domain Built in (deployed by Azure when Apim is deployed) and replace it with our Custom Domain Gateway declared in the TF Configuration file. This is because when terraform refresh the APIM, it detect two custom domain and will place in list 0 the custom domain built in created by Azure and in list 1 the custom domain gateway provided in tf file. It does not have a major impact but will slow the tf build on each apply and pollute the terraform plan. 

To fixe this "issue" i've had to explicitly declare the Custom Domain Built In from Azure in the Tf Configuration file, it is for sure not the best solution as it should not be present in the terraform configuration file because it is a custom domain managed by Azure  :

    proxy {
      host_name = "Azure Custom Domain Built in"
    }

    proxy {
      host_name = "our custom domain"
      certificate = XXX
    }

This fixe the issue but terraform should not refresh the Azure Custom Domain Built in and place it in list 0

### Description

The azurerm_web_application_firewall_policy resource does not support and is unaware of the State property on the CustomRule present from API Version (2022-09-01). 

- This is an issue as you can't add this property to an ignore_changes block on this resource
- It does not capture the current state of a custom rule 
- Could potentially result in it being re-enabled whilst not indicating so in the terraform plan

See:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.azure.commands.network.models.psapplicationgatewayfirewallcustomrule?view=az-ps-latest

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/application-gateway/web-application-firewall-policies/list?tabs=HTTP
```
        "customRules": [
          {
            "name": "Rule1",
            "priority": 1,
            "state": "Enabled",
            "ruleType": "MatchRule",
            "matchConditions": [
              {
                "matchVariables": [
                  {
                    "variableName": "RemoteAddr",
                    "selector": null
                  }
                ],
                "operator": "IPMatch",
                "negationConditon": false,
                "matchValues": [
                  "192.168.1.0/24",
                  "10.0.0.0/24"
                ],
                "transforms": []
              }
            ],
            "action": "Block"
          },

```

Is it just a matter of adding the state as a item here? or are we limited by API version the provider is using?
terraform-provider-azurerm/internal/services/network/web_application_firewall_policy_resource.go

```
func expandWebApplicationFirewallPolicyWebApplicationFirewallCustomRule(input []interface{}) *[]webapplicationfirewallpolicies.WebApplicationFirewallCustomRule {
	results := make([]webapplicationfirewallpolicies.WebApplicationFirewallCustomRule, 0)
	for _, item := range input {
		v := item.(map[string]interface{})
		name := v["name"].(string)
		priority := v["priority"].(int)
		ruleType := v["rule_type"].(string)
		matchConditions := v["match_conditions"].([]interface{})
		action := v["action"].(string)

		result := webapplicationfirewallpolicies.WebApplicationFirewallCustomRule{
			Action:          webapplicationfirewallpolicies.WebApplicationFirewallAction(action),
			MatchConditions: expandWebApplicationFirewallPolicyMatchCondition(matchConditions),
			Name:            pointer.To(name),
			Priority:        int64(priority),
			RuleType:        webapplicationfirewallpolicies.WebApplicationFirewallRuleType(ruleType),
		}

		results = append(results, result)
	}
	return &results
}
```

### Terraform (and AzureRM Provider) Version

Terraform v0.12.18

+ provider.random v2.2.1

### Affected Resource(s)

* `azurerm_nat_gateway`
* `azurerm_virtual_machine_extension`

### Terraform Configuration Files

```hcl
git clone https://github.com/sdcscripts/issue_with_nat
cd issue_with_nat
mv terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
terraform init
terraform apply 
terraform destroy
```
During the destroy always get the following 

Error: Code="RetryableError" Message="A retryable error occurred."

### Expected Behavior

Should have created all resources and then the destroy should have destroyed all resources

### Actual Behavior

Create happens fine but the destroy fails every time. 

### Steps to Reproduce

git clone https://github.com/sdcscripts/issue_with_nat
cd issue_with_nat
mv terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars
terraform init
terraform apply 
terraform destroy

### Important Factoids

I have managed to resolve the problem by using a depends_on with the natgw module , in effect stopping the NAT G/W resources being created before the VMextensions are created and enforcing that the NAT G/W is deleted before the VMextension resources. This resolves the problem so it's basically some kind of race condition / deadlock with NAT G/W and VM extension on destroy operation that causes the "retryable error".

The retryable error sometimes does not allow a repeat terraform destroy because the state file becomes corrupted.

terraform plan/apply should detect a configuration drift (sub-resource "private_service_connection" is broken)

no configuration change is detected (see output from "terraform plan" above)

### Steps to Reproduce

Prerequisites:

- VNet with subnet to create private endpoint in
- Private DNS zone for "privatelink.database.windows.net"

Steps to reproduce:

1. create resources (RG, SQL Server, Private Endpoint) with terraform code shown above ("terraform apply"). It will also create
   * PEP with Connection Status "Approved"
   * A-record for "sql-pep-tf-bug" is created in private zone "privatelink.database.windows.net"
   * network interface gets created (to hold the private IP)
2. action in Azure Portal
   * got to "SQL servers", select "sql-pep-tf-bug", go to Networking  -> Private access,
   * select the one private endpoint (pep-pep-tf-bug)  and click "Remove" (and confirm)
3. Checks in Azure Portal
   * Private Endpoint "pep-pep-tf-bug" will now show Connection status "Disconnected"
   * A-record for  "sql-pep-tf-bug" is not longer present in private zone "privatelink.database.windows.net"
4. Now run "terraform plan" => no change is detected ("terraform refresh") does not help

Workaround:  "taint" the azurerm_private_endpoint resource and re-run "terraform apply". That will re-created the PEP and fix the situation.

The main issue is the fact that the provider does not detect any configuration drift in that situation.

### Description

The `azurerm_key_vault_access_policy` resource currently does not accept `all` for certificates, keys, secrets and storage permissions:

> Error: expected key_permissions.0 to be one of [Backup Create Decrypt Delete Encrypt Get Import List Purge Recover Restore Sign UnwrapKey Update Verify WrapKey Release Rotate GetRotationPolicy SetRotationPolicy], got **all**

According to the [Azure Documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/templates/microsoft.keyvault/vaults/accesspolicies?pivots=deployment-language-bicep#permissions) its a valid value.

This makes writing an access policy that enables every permission cumbersome. Also, it leads to existing access policies that use the `all` permission being destroyed on import because a change is detected.

### Loadbalancer configuration

  location            = var.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.rg.name
  sku                 = "Standard"

    name                          = "LoadBalancerFrontEnd"
    private_ip_address_allocation = "Static"
    subnet_id                     = data.azurerm_subnet.indexer.id
    private_ip_address_version    = "IPv4"
    private_ip_address            = var.indexer_lb_private_ip
  }
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [
      tags
    ]
  }
}
```
The plan output (redacting most of the plan) when altering a different resource (i.e. the loadbalancer was already created and I had changed a different resource entirely): 
```
# azurerm_lb.indexer must be replaced
-/+ resource "azurerm_lb" "indexer" {
      ~ id                   = "*****" -> (known after apply)
        location             = "northeurope"
        name                 = "prdindexer-lb"
      ~ private_ip_address   = ****-> (known after apply)
      ~ private_ip_addresses = [
          - ****,
        ] -> (known after apply)
        resource_group_name  = "****"
        sku                  = "Standard"

~ frontend_ip_configuration {
          ~ id                            = "****" -> (known after apply)
          ~ inbound_nat_rules             = [] -> (known after apply)
          ~ load_balancer_rules           = [
              - "*****",
            ] -> (known after apply)
            name                          = "LoadBalancerFrontEnd"
          ~ outbound_rules                = [] -> (known after apply)
            private_ip_address            = "****"
          ~ private_ip_address_allocation = "Static" -> "static"
            private_ip_address_version    = "IPv4"
          + public_ip_address_id          = (known after apply)
          + public_ip_prefix_id           = (known after apply)
            subnet_id                     = "*****"
          - zones                         = [
              - "1",
              - "2",
              - "3",
            ] -> null # forces replacement
        }
    }

```
When adding `frontend_ip_configuration[0].zones` - the lb resource does not get recreated (as per tf plan). 

On previous versions of the provider - our pipelines ran and lb were not being recreated. This I believe is because, as per docs, when Zones is not specified (like in my configuration), the loadbalancer would be zone redundant. However, now it is following the new zone behaviour change (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-gb/updates/zone-behavior-change/) and when not specifying zone a non-zonal resource is created. 

You are also not able to specify zones = `["1","2","3"]`

resource "azurerm_virtual_machine_extension" "test" {
  name                             = "TestConfigScript"
  location                         = azurerm_resource_group.test.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.test.name
  virtual_machine_name = azurerm_virtual_machine.test.name
  publisher                       = "Microsoft.Azure.Extensions"
  type                                = "CustomScript"
  type_handler_version    = "2.0"

  settings = jsonencode(
    {
      commandToExecute = "touch ~/foo"
    }
  )
}



```
### Expected Behavior


When the VM needs to be replaced I would expect the provider to:

1. Destroy the vm extension
2. Destroy the vm
3. Create the VM
4. Create the VM extension

### Actual Behavior

Only the VM is explicitly destroyed.  Since the VM extension is attached to the vm, it is never recreated and will not run on the VM.  The vm extension has to be manually tainted whenever a VM needs to be replaced.

### Steps to Reproduce

```
terraform init
terraform apply -auto-approve
terraform taint azurerm_virtual_machine.test
terraform apply -auto-approve
```

### Workaround

This behaviour seems to occur because the only link in the DAG is to the `name` property of the virtual machine.  Since this is usually static and not computed, terraform doesn't 'know' that the resource needs to be replaced on the same lifecycle as the virtual machine.  Forcing this connection by manually parsing the vm name from its id gives me the behaviour I would expect.

```
virtual_machine_name = split("virtualMachines/", azurerm_virtual_machine.test.id)[1]
```

I would suggest the `virtual_machine_name` property be deprecated and replaced with virtual_machine_id and have the provider parse the vm name to pass to api.

I would be happy to provide a pull request if this is an appropriate solution.
