### Description

Currently, the `azurerm_lb` resource allows multiple front_ip_configuration blocks to be defined within it.  However, as they are "embeded" in the resource, you are unable to use a count to control how many addresses get created. 

### Affected Resource(s)

Key scenario this becomes an issue is in supporting multiple zones.  Take the following configuration:

```
resource "azurerm_lb" "mylb" {
  name                = "my-lb"
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.main.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.main.name

  frontend_ip_configuration {
    name                          = "${azurerm_resource_group.main.name}-lb-ip"
    subnet_id                     = data.azurerm_subnet.subnet.id
    private_ip_address_allocation = "dynamic"
  }
```

The above scenario is simple enough: a LB with a single internal IP.  If I want to support something across multiple zones, however, I have to now duplicate the `frontend_ip_configuration` for every zone.  This becomes really troublesome if I setup a list or map of the zones so the admin can select which zones/how many he actually wants to use (maybe the service is fine in only 2 zones .... maybe the region selected only has 1).

This becomes really complicated really fast.

<!--- Please list the new or affected resources and data sources. --->



### Potential Terraform Configuration

**azurerm_lb_frontend_ip_configuration**
This mimics what's done in a lot of other scenarios (including backend ip association). A seperate resource black that can be associated and thus, allows us to use counts to control quantity.

```
resource "azurerm_lb" "managerlb" {
  name                = "${azurerm_resource_group.main.name}-lb"
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.main.location
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.main.name

}

resource "azurerm_lb_frontend_ip_configuration" "ips" {
  count =  3
  loadbalancer_id = azurerm_lb.managerlb.id
  name = "lb-ip-zone-${count.index +1}"
  subnet_id  = data.azurerm_subnet.subnet.id
  private_ip_address_allocation = "dynamic"
  zones   = [count.index + 1]
}
```

This is obviously over simplified, but it now gives me the ability to set a scalable count that spans zones easily.

I try to explain in a few words. You should enter the _name_ of the public IP address and _resource_group_name_ arguments to fetch an _ip_address_ attribute. ### Description

<!--- Please leave a helpful description of the feature request here. --->

I don't know if this is something that's possible to fix in the azurerm provider. It might be that it's a kind of thing that needs to be supported in Azure first. So I apologize in advance if this issue is misplaced.

On most resources in the `azuread` provider, there is the following note:

> NOTE: If you're authenticating using a Service Principal then it must have permissions to both `Read and write owned by applications` and `Sign in and read user profile` within the `Windows Azure Active Directory API`.

If you want to use Terraform to set up an application that has those permissions, it's pretty straightforward using the `required_resource_access` block in the `azuread_application` resource. However, if you want to authenticate to the `azuread` provider using a service principal that belongs to a Managed Identity, things get very tricky. The only way that I found to set up those permissions is to:

1. Create a managed identity and get its service principal id
2. Run the `New-AzureADServiceAppRoleAssignment` powershell cmdlet to add the `Application.ReadWrite.All` permission, referencing the principal id from step 1
3. In the Azure AD Microsoft Graph API, send a POST to oauth2PermissionGrants, referencing the principal id from step 1

Of course it would be much easier to do all of this in Terraform.

I think this might be impossible though, because:
* When you create an Application through the Azure Portal, you get a bunch of options for API access. It seems this is what correlates to the `required_resource_access` block in `azuread_application`.
* When you create a Managed Identity through the Azure Portal, there's nowhere to specify any sort of Microsoft Graph API permissions. It seems this isn't something that the Azure Resource Manager really supports...
* There's a role in Azure AD called `Application Administrator` that I think should allow users to add Microsoft Graph permissions to Applications. However, when I was trying to add permissions directly to a Managed Identity's service principal, I pretty much needed Global Administrator (at least needed Privileged Role Administrator). So I think `Application Administrator` might only apply to applications, not to service principals.

I'm mostly creating this issue because I'm curious if my hunch is correct that this is a pain point coming from upstream.
